10.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
budhasya tu muniśreṣṭhā vidvān putraḥ purūravāḥ
tejasvī dānaśīlaś ca yajvā vipuladakṣiṇaḥ //
10.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
बुधस्य तु मुनिश्रेष्ठा विद्वान् पुत्रः पुरूरवाः
तेजस्वी दानशीलश् च यज्वा विपुलदक्षिणः ॥
10.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / The son of Budha, O best of sages, was the wise Purūravas, / radiant, generous, a sacrificer who gave abundant sacrificial gifts,

10.s:
brahmavādī parākrāntaḥ śatrubhir yudhi durdamaḥ
āhartā cāgnihotrasya yajñānāṃ ca mahīpatiḥ //
10.d:
ब्रह्मवादी पराक्रान्तः शत्रुभिर् युधि दुर्दमः
आहर्ता चाग्निहोत्रस्य यज्ञानां च महीपतिः ॥
10.m: an expounder of the Veda, valiant, difficult to subdue by enemies in battle, / the maintainer of the agnihotra and performer of sacrifices, a lord of the earth,

10.s:
satyavādī puṇyamatiḥ samyaksaṃvṛtamaithunaḥ
atīva triṣu lokeṣu yaśasāpratimaḥ sadā //
10.d:
सत्यवादी पुण्यमतिः सम्यक्संवृतमैथुनः
अतीव त्रिषु लोकेषु यशसाप्रतिमः सदा ॥
10.m: truthful, virtuous in mind, properly restrained in sexual enjoyment, / ever unequaled in fame throughout the three worlds.

10.s:
taṃ brahmavādinaṃ śāntaṃ dharmajñaṃ satyavādinam
urvaśī varayām āsa hitvā mānaṃ yaśasvinī //
10.d:
तं ब्रह्मवादिनं शान्तं धर्मज्ञं सत्यवादिनम्
उर्वशी वरयाम् आस हित्वा मानं यशस्विनी ॥
10.m: Him—the peaceful, expounder of the Veda, knower of dharma, truthful in speech— / the renowned Urvaśī chose [as husband], casting aside pride.

10.s:
tayā sahāvasad rājā daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca
ṣaṭ pañca sapta cāṣṭau ca daśa cāṣṭau ca bho dvijāḥ //
10.d:
तया सहावसद् राजा दश वर्षाणि पञ्च च
षट् पञ्च सप्त चाष्टौ च दश चाष्टौ च भो द्विजाः ॥
10.m: The king lived with her for ten years and five, / and six, five, seven, and eight, and ten and eight, O twice-born ones,

10.s:
vane caitrarathe ramye tathā mandākinītaṭe
alakāyāṃ viśālāyāṃ nandane ca vanottame //
10.d:
वने चैत्ररथे रम्ये तथा मन्दाकिनीतटे
अलकायां विशालायां नन्दने च वनोत्तमे ॥
10.m: in the delightful Caitraratha forest, likewise on the bank of the Mandākinī, / in spacious Alakā, and in the excellent Nandana grove;

10.s:
uttarān sa kurūn prāpya manoramaphaladrumān
gandhamādanapādeṣu meruśṛṅge tathottare //
10.d:
उत्तरान् स कुरून् प्राप्य मनोरमफलद्रुमान्
गन्धमादनपादेषु मेरुशृङ्गे तथोत्तरे ॥
10.m: reaching the Northern Kurus with their pleasant fruit-bearing trees, / on the slopes of Gandhamādana, and likewise on the northern peak of Meru.

10.s:
eteṣu vanamukhyeṣu surair ācariteṣu ca
urvaśyā sahito rājā reme paramayā mudā //
10.d:
एतेषु वनमुख्येषु सुरैर् आचरितेषु च
उर्वश्या सहितो राजा रेमे परमया मुदा ॥
10.m: In these principal forests frequented by gods, / the king, accompanied by Urvaśī, delighted with supreme joy.

10.s:
deśe puṇyatame caiva maharṣibhir abhiṣṭute
rājyaṃ sa kārayām āsa prayāge pṛthivīpatiḥ //
10.d:
देशे पुण्यतमे चैव महर्षिभिर् अभिष्टुते
राज्यं स कारयाम् आस प्रयागे पृथिवीपतिः ॥
10.m: And in the most holy region, praised by great sages, / at Prayāga, the lord of the earth ruled his kingdom.

10.s:
evaṃprabhāvo rājāsīd ailas tu narasattamaḥ
uttare jāhnavītīre pratiṣṭhāne mahāyaśāḥ //
10.d:
एवंप्रभावो राजासीद् ऐलस् तु नरसत्तमः
उत्तरे जाह्नवीतीरे प्रतिष्ठाने महायशाः ॥
10.m: Such was the king’s majesty, that son of Ilā, best among men, / renowned, at Pratiṣṭhāna on the north bank of the Ganges.

10.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
ailaputrā babhūvus te sapta devasutopamāḥ
gandharvaloke viditā āyur dhīmān amāvasuḥ //
10.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
ऐलपुत्रा बभूवुस् ते सप्त देवसुतोपमाः
गन्धर्वलोके विदिता आयुर् धीमान् अमावसुः ॥
10.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / The sons of the son of Ilā were seven, equal to sons of the gods, / known in the world of the Gandharvas: the wise Āyus, Amāvasu,

10.s:
viśvāyuś caiva dharmātmā śrutāyuś ca tathāparaḥ
dṛḍhāyuś ca vanāyuś ca bahvāyuś corvaśīsutāḥ //
10.d:
विश्वायुश् चैव धर्मात्मा श्रुतायुश् च तथापरः
दृढायुश् च वनायुश् च बह्वायुश् चोर्वशीसुताः ॥
10.m: the righteous Viśvāyus, and likewise another, Śrutāyus, / Dṛḍhāyus, Vanāyus, and Bahvāyus, the sons of Urvaśī.

10.s:
amāvasos tu dāyādo bhīmo rājātha rājarāṭ
śrīmān bhīmasya dāyādo rājāsīt kāñcanaprabhaḥ //
10.d:
अमावसोस् तु दायादो भीमो राजाथ राजराट्
श्रीमान् भीमस्य दायादो राजासीत् काञ्चनप्रभः ॥
10.m: The heir of Amāvasu was King Bhīma, a king of kings; / the glorious heir of Bhīma was King Kāñcanaprabha.

10.s:
vidvāṃs tu kāñcanasyāpi suhotro 'bhūn mahābalaḥ
suhotrasyābhavaj jahnuḥ keśinyā garbhasaṃbhavaḥ //
10.d:
विद्वांस् तु काञ्चनस्यापि सुहोत्रो ऽभून् महाबलः
सुहोत्रस्याभवज् जह्नुः केशिन्या गर्भसंभवः ॥
10.m: The son of Kāñcana was the wise and mighty Suhotra; / Suhotra had Jahnu, born from the womb of Keśinī,

10.s:
ājahre yo mahat sattraṃ sarpamedhaṃ mahāmakham
patilobhena yaṃ gaṅgā patitvena sasāra ha //
10.d:
आजह्रे यो महत् सत्त्रं सर्पमेधं महामखम्
पतिलोभेन यं गङ्गा पतित्वेन ससार ह ॥
10.m: who performed the great sacrificial session, the great snake-sacrifice; / whom the Ganges pursued as a husband out of longing for him as her lord.

10.s:
necchataḥ plāvayām āsa tasya gaṅgā tadā sadaḥ
sa tayā plāvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñavāṭaṃ samantataḥ //
10.d:
नेच्छतः प्लावयाम् आस तस्य गङ्गा तदा सदः
स तया प्लावितं दृष्ट्वा यज्ञवाटं समन्ततः ॥
10.m: When he did not desire her, the Ganges then flooded his sacrificial hall; / seeing his sacrificial enclosure flooded completely by her,

10.s:
sauhotrir aśapad gaṅgāṃ kruddho rājā dvijottamāḥ
eṣa te viphalaṃ yatnaṃ pibann ambhaḥ karomy aham //
10.d:
सौहोत्रिर् अशपद् गङ्गां क्रुद्धो राजा द्विजोत्तमाः
एष ते विफलं यत्नं पिबन्न् अम्भः करोम्य् अहम् ॥
10.m: the son of Suhotra, an enraged king, O best of twice-born ones, cursed the Ganges: / “Drinking up your water, I shall make this effort of yours futile!

10.s:
asya gaṅge 'valepasya sadyaḥ phalam avāpnuhi
jahnurājarṣiṇā pītāṃ gaṅgāṃ dṛṣṭvā maharṣayaḥ //
10.d:
अस्य गङ्गे ऽवलेपस्य सद्यः फलम् अवाप्नुहि
जह्नुराजर्षिणा पीतां गङ्गां दृष्ट्वा महर्षयः ॥
10.m: O Ganges, reap immediately the fruit of this arrogance!” / Seeing the Ganges swallowed by the royal sage Jahnu, the great sages

10.s:
upaninyur mahābhāgāṃ duhitṛtvena jāhnavīm
yuvanāśvasya putrīṃ tu kāverīṃ jahnur āvahat //
10.d:
उपनिन्युर् महाभागां दुहितृत्वेन जाह्नवीम्
युवनाश्वस्य पुत्रीं तु कावेरीं जह्नुर् आवहत् ॥
10.m: brought the highly fortunate daughter of Jahnu as his daughter. / Jahnu married Kāverī, the daughter of Yuvanāśva,

10.s:
yuvanāśvasya śāpena gaṅgārdhena vinirgatā
kāverīṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ jahnor bhāryām aninditām //
10.d:
युवनाश्वस्य शापेन गङ्गार्धेन विनिर्गता
कावेरीं सरितां श्रेष्ठां जह्नोर् भार्याम् अनिन्दिताम् ॥
10.m: who, by the curse of Yuvanāśva, emerged with half of the Ganges— / Kāverī, the best of rivers, Jahnu’s blameless wife.

10.s:
jahnus tu dayitaṃ putraṃ sunadyaṃ nāma dhārmikam
kāveryāṃ janayām āsa ajakas tasya cātmajaḥ //
10.d:
जह्नुस् तु दयितं पुत्रं सुनद्यं नाम धार्मिकम्
कावेर्यां जनयाम् आस अजकस् तस्य चात्मजः ॥
10.m: And Jahnu begot upon Kāverī a beloved, righteous son / named Sunadya; and Ajaka was his son.

10.s:
ajakasya tu dāyādo balākāśvo mahīpatiḥ
babhūva mṛgayāśīlaḥ kuśas tasyātmajo 'bhavat //
10.d:
अजकस्य तु दायादो बलाकाश्वो महीपतिः
बभूव मृगयाशीलः कुशस् तस्यात्मजो ऽभवत् ॥
10.m: The heir of Ajaka was King Balākāśva, / who was fond of hunting; Kuśa was his son.

10.s:
kuśaputrā babhūvur hi catvāro devavarcasaḥ
kuśikaḥ kuśanābhaś ca kuśāmbo mūrtimāṃs tathā //
10.d:
कुशपुत्रा बभूवुर् हि चत्वारो देववर्चसः
कुशिकः कुशनाभश् च कुशाम्बो मूर्तिमांस् तथा ॥
10.m: Four sons indeed were born to Kuśa, possessing divine luster: / Kuśika, Kuśanābha, Kuśāmba, and Mūrtimat.

10.s:
ballavaiḥ saha saṃvṛddho rājā vanacaraḥ sadā
kuśikas tu tapas tepe putram indrasamaṃ prabhuḥ //
10.d:
बल्लवैः सह संवृद्धो राजा वनचरः सदा
कुशिकस् तु तपस् तेपे पुत्रम् इन्द्रसमं प्रभुः ॥
10.m: Grown up among cowherds, the lord was ever a king roaming the forest; / and Kuśika performed austerities, wishing: “May I obtain a son equal to Indra.”

10.s:
labheyam iti taṃ śakras trāsād abhyetya jajñivān
pūrṇe varṣasahasre vai tataḥ śakro hy apaśyata //
10.d:
लभेयम् इति तं शक्रस् त्रासाद् अभ्येत्य जज्ञिवान्
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे वै ततः शक्रो ह्य् अपश्यत ॥
10.m: Out of fear, Śakra approached and took birth [as his son]; / indeed, when a thousand years were completed, Śakra then beheld him.

10.s:
atyugratapasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
samarthaḥ putrajanane svayam evāsya śāśvataḥ //
10.d:
अत्युग्रतपसं दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः
समर्थः पुत्रजनने स्वयम् एवास्य शाश्वतः ॥
10.m: Seeing him engaged in extremely severe austerities, the thousand-eyed Puraṃdara, / capable himself of fathering a son for him, the eternal one,

10.s:
putrārthaṃ kalpayām āsa devendraḥ surasattamaḥ
sa gādhir abhavad rājā maghavān kauśikaḥ svayam //
10.d:
पुत्रार्थं कल्पयाम् आस देवेन्द्रः सुरसत्तमः
स गाधिर् अभवद् राजा मघवान् कौशिकः स्वयम् ॥
10.m: the ruler of the gods, the best of deities, prepared himself to become the son; / Maghavat Kauśika himself became King Gādhi.

10.s:
paurā yasyābhavad bhāryā gādhis tasyām ajāyata
gādheḥ kanyā mahābhāgā nāmnā satyavatī śubhā //
10.d:
पौरा यस्याभवद् भार्या गाधिस् तस्याम् अजायत
गाधेः कन्या महाभागा नाम्ना सत्यवती शुभा ॥
10.m: Paurā was his wife, upon whom Gādhi was born; / Gādhi had an auspicious, highly fortunate daughter named Satyavatī.

10.s:
tāṃ gādhiḥ kāvyaputrāya ṛcīkāya dadau prabhuḥ
tasyāḥ prītaḥ sa vai bhartā bhārgavo bhṛgunandanaḥ //
10.d:
तां गाधिः काव्यपुत्राय ऋचीकाय ददौ प्रभुः
तस्याः प्रीतः स वै भर्ता भार्गवो भृगुनन्दनः ॥
10.m: The lord Gādhi gave her to Ṛcīka, the son of Kāvya; / pleased with her was that husband of hers, the Bhārgava, descendant of Bhṛgu.

10.s:
putrārthaṃ sādhayām āsa caruṃ gādhes tathaiva ca
uvācāhūya tāṃ bhāryām ṛcīko bhārgavas tadā //
10.d:
पुत्रार्थं साधयाम् आस चरुं गाधेस् तथैव च
उवाचाहूय तां भार्याम् ऋचीको भार्गवस् तदा ॥
10.m: For the sake of a son, Ṛcīka, the descendant of Bhṛgu, then prepared a sacrificial offering for her and also for Gādhi. / Calling his wife, he then spoke to her:

10.s:
upayojyaś carur ayaṃ tvayā mātrā svayaṃ śubhe
tasyāṃ janiṣyate putro dīptimān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ //
10.d:
उपयोज्यश् चरुर् अयं त्वया मात्रा स्वयं शुभे
तस्यां जनिष्यते पुत्रो दीप्तिमान् क्षत्रियर्षभः ॥
10.m: "This sacrificial offering is to be consumed by you, and [the other] by your mother, O auspicious one. / From her, a radiant son shall be born, a bull among kṣatriyas,

10.s:
ajeyaḥ kṣatriyair loke kṣatriyarṣabhasūdanaḥ
tavāpi putraṃ kalyāṇi dhṛtimantaṃ tapodhanam //
10.d:
अजेयः क्षत्रियैर् लोके क्षत्रियर्षभसूदनः
तवापि पुत्रं कल्याणि धृतिमन्तं तपोधनम् ॥
10.m: unconquerable by kṣatriyas in the world, a slayer of the bulls among kṣatriyas; / and for you too, O blessed one, [shall be born] a son steadfast and rich in ascetic power,

10.s:
śamātmakaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ carur eṣa vidhāsyati
evam uktvā tu tāṃ bhāryām ṛcīko bhṛgunandanaḥ //
10.d:
शमात्मकं द्विजश्रेष्ठं चरुर् एष विधास्यति
एवम् उक्त्वा तु तां भार्याम् ऋचीको भृगुनन्दनः ॥
10.m: endowed with tranquility, the best of the twice-born; this sacrificial offering shall bring this about." / Having thus spoken to his wife, Ṛcīka, the joy of Bhṛgu,

10.s:
tapasy abhirato nityam araṇyaṃ praviveśa ha
gādhiḥ sadāras tu tadā ṛcīkāśramam abhyagāt //
10.d:
तपस्य् अभिरतो नित्यम् अरण्यं प्रविवेश ह
गाधिः सदारस् तु तदा ऋचीकाश्रमम् अभ्यगात् ॥
10.m: always devoted to austerity, entered the forest. / Then Gādhi, accompanied by his wife, came to Ṛcīka's hermitage,

10.s:
tīrthayātrāprasaṅgena sutāṃ draṣṭuṃ nareśvaraḥ
carudvayaṃ gṛhītvā sā ṛṣeḥ satyavatī tadā //
10.d:
तीर्थयात्राप्रसङ्गेन सुतां द्रष्टुं नरेश्वरः
चरुद्वयं गृहीत्वा सा ऋषेः सत्यवती तदा ॥
10.m: the king [having come] on the occasion of a pilgrimage to sacred sites to see his daughter. / Taking the two sacrificial offerings of the sage, Satyavatī then,

10.s:
carum ādāya yatnena sā tu mātre nyavedayat
mātā tu tasyā daivena duhitre svaṃ caruṃ dadau //
10.d:
चरुम् आदाय यत्नेन सा तु मात्रे न्यवेदयत्
माता तु तस्या दैवेन दुहित्रे स्वं चरुं ददौ ॥
10.m: carefully taking the offering, offered it to her mother; / but her mother, through fate, gave her own offering to her daughter,

10.s:
tasyāś carum athājñānād ātmasaṃsthaṃ cakāra ha
atha satyavatī sarvaṃ kṣatriyāntakaraṃ tadā //
10.d:
तस्याश् चरुम् अथाज्ञानाद् आत्मसंस्थं चकार ह
अथ सत्यवती सर्वं क्षत्रियान्तकरं तदा ॥
10.m: and out of ignorance appropriated her [daughter's] offering for herself. / Then Satyavatī, bearing all that would bring about the destruction of kṣatriyas,

10.s:
dhārayām āsa dīptena vapuṣā ghoradarśanā
tām ṛcīkas tato dṛṣṭvā yogenābhyupasṛtya ca //
10.d:
धारयाम् आस दीप्तेन वपुषा घोरदर्शना
ताम् ऋचीकस् ततो दृष्ट्वा योगेनाभ्युपसृत्य च ॥
10.m: became terrifying in appearance with her glowing body. / Then Ṛcīka, seeing her and approaching through yogic power,

10.s:
tato 'bravīd dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ svāṃ bhāryāṃ varavarṇinīm
mātrāsi vañcitā bhadre caruvyatyāsahetunā //
10.d:
ततो ऽब्रवीद् द्विजश्रेष्ठः स्वां भार्यां वरवर्णिनीम्
मात्रासि वञ्चिता भद्रे चरुव्यत्यासहेतुना ॥
10.m: the best of the twice-born then said to his wife of excellent complexion: / "You have been deceived by your mother, O blessed lady, by the switching of the offerings.

10.s:
janayiṣyati hi putras te krūrakarmātidāruṇaḥ
bhrātā janiṣyate cāpi brahmabhūtas tapodhanaḥ //
10.d:
जनयिष्यति हि पुत्रस् ते क्रूरकर्मातिदारुणः
भ्राता जनिष्यते चापि ब्रह्मभूतस् तपोधनः ॥
10.m: For your son will perform cruel deeds and be extremely fierce; / and your brother shall be born as one who has become brahman, rich in ascetic power.

10.s:
viśvaṃ hi brahma tapasā mayā tasmin samarpitam
evam uktā mahābhāgā bhartrā satyavatī tadā //
10.d:
विश्वं हि ब्रह्म तपसा मया तस्मिन् समर्पितम्
एवम् उक्ता महाभागा भर्त्रा सत्यवती तदा ॥
10.m: For through austerity I had infused the entire brahmanhood into that [offering]." / Having been spoken to thus by her husband, the illustrious Satyavatī then

10.s:
prasādayām āsa patiṃ putro me nedṛśo bhavet
brāhmaṇāpasadas tvatta ity ukto munir abravīt //
10.d:
प्रसादयाम् आस पतिं पुत्रो मे नेदृशो भवेत्
ब्राह्मणापसदस् त्वत्त इत्य् उक्तो मुनिर् अब्रवीत् ॥
10.m: propitiated her husband: "May my son not be like this, / a disgrace to brāhmaṇas born from you!" Spoken to thus, the sage said:

10.s:
ṛcīka uvāca
naiṣa saṃkalpitaḥ kāmo mayā bhadre tathāstv iti
ugrakarmā bhavet putraḥ pitur mātuś ca kāraṇāt //
10.d:
ऋचीक उवाच
नैष संकल्पितः कामो मया भद्रे तथास्त्व् इति
उग्रकर्मा भवेत् पुत्रः पितुर् मातुश् च कारणात् ॥
10.m: Ṛcīka said: / "This wish was not conceived by me as 'May it be so,' O blessed one. / The son would be of fierce deeds because of the father and the mother."

10.s:
punaḥ satyavatī vākyam evam uktvābravīd idam
icchaṃl lokān api mune sṛjethāḥ kiṃ punaḥ sutam //
10.d:
पुनः सत्यवती वाक्यम् एवम् उक्त्वाब्रवीद् इदम्
इच्छंल् लोकान् अपि मुने सृजेथाः किं पुनः सुतम् ॥
10.m: Satyavatī spoke this word again after he had said this: / "If you wish, O sage, you could create even whole worlds, so what of a son?

10.s:
śamātmakam ṛjuṃ tvaṃ me putraṃ dātum ihārhasi
kāmam evaṃvidhaḥ pautro mama syāt tava ca prabho //
10.d:
शमात्मकम् ऋजुं त्वं मे पुत्रं दातुम् इहार्हसि
कामम् एवंविधः पौत्रो मम स्यात् तव च प्रभो ॥
10.m: You ought to grant me here a son who is tranquil and upright. / Let such a one be, if you will, my grandson and yours, O lord,

10.s:
yady anyathā na śakyaṃ vai kartum etad dvijottama
tataḥ prasādam akarot sa tasyās tapaso balāt //
10.d:
यद्य् अन्यथा न शक्यं वै कर्तुम् एतद् द्विजोत्तम
ततः प्रसादम् अकरोत् स तस्यास् तपसो बलात् ॥
10.m: if it is indeed impossible to make this otherwise, O best of the twice-born." / Then, by the power of his austerity, he granted her favor:

10.s:
putre nāsti viśeṣo me pautre vā varavarṇini
tvayā yathoktaṃ vacanaṃ tathā bhadre bhaviṣyati //
10.d:
पुत्रे नास्ति विशेषो मे पौत्रे वा वरवर्णिनि
त्वया यथोक्तं वचनं तथा भद्रे भविष्यति ॥
10.m: "There is no distinction for me between a son and a grandson, O lady of excellent complexion. / As was spoken by you, so it shall be, O blessed lady."

10.s:
tataḥ satyavatī putraṃ janayām āsa bhārgavam
tapasy abhirataṃ dāntaṃ jamadagniṃ samātmakam //
10.d:
ततः सत्यवती पुत्रं जनयाम् आस भार्गवम्
तपस्य् अभिरतं दान्तं जमदग्निं समात्मकम् ॥
10.m: Then Satyavatī gave birth to a son of the Bhṛgu lineage, / devoted to austerity, restrained, Jamadagni, endowed with tranquility.

10.s:
bhṛgor jagatyāṃ vaṃśe 'smiñ jamadagnir ajāyata
sā hi satyavatī puṇyā satyadharmaparāyaṇā //
10.d:
भृगोर् जगत्यां वंशे ऽस्मिञ् जमदग्निर् अजायत
सा हि सत्यवती पुण्या सत्यधर्मपरायणा ॥
10.m: In this lineage of Bhṛgu upon the earth Jamadagni was born. / That holy Satyavatī, devoted to truth and dharma,

10.s:
kauśikīti samākhyātā pravṛtteyaṃ mahānadī
ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavo reṇur nāma narādhipaḥ //
10.d:
कौशिकीति समाख्याता प्रवृत्तेयं महानदी
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रेणुर् नाम नराधिपः ॥
10.m: became this great river famed as Kauśikī. / A king named Reṇu was born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku;

10.s:
tasya kanyā mahābhāgā kāmalī nāma reṇukā
reṇukāyāṃ tu kāmalyāṃ tapovidyāsamanvitaḥ //
10.d:
तस्य कन्या महाभागा कामली नाम रेणुका
रेणुकायां तु कामल्यां तपोविद्यासमन्वितः ॥
10.m: his daughter was the illustrious Reṇukā, also called Kāmalī. / Upon Reṇukā Kāmalī, the son of Ṛcīka, endowed with austerity and learning,

10.s:
ārcīko janayām āsa jāmadagnyaṃ sudāruṇam
sarvavidyāntagaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanurvedasya pāragam //
10.d:
आर्चीको जनयाम् आस जामदग्न्यं सुदारुणम्
सर्वविद्यान्तगं श्रेष्ठं धनुर्वेदस्य पारगम् ॥
10.m: fathered the son of Jamadagni, who was exceedingly terrible, / who had mastered all sciences, the best, adept in the science of archery,

10.s:
rāmaṃ kṣatriyahantāraṃ pradīptam iva pāvakam
aurvasyaivam ṛcīkasya satyavatyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ //
10.d:
रामं क्षत्रियहन्तारं प्रदीप्तम् इव पावकम्
और्वस्यैवम् ऋचीकस्य सत्यवत्यां महायशाः ॥
10.m: Rāma, the slayer of kṣatriyas, like a blazing fire. / Thus to Ṛcīka, son of Ūrva, upon Satyavatī, of great renown,

10.s:
jamadagnis tapovīryāj jajñe brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
madhyamaś ca śunaḥśephaḥ śunaḥpucchaḥ kaniṣṭhakaḥ //
10.d:
जमदग्निस् तपोवीर्याज् जज्ञे ब्रह्मविदां वरः
मध्यमश् च शुनःशेफः शुनःपुच्छः कनिष्ठकः ॥
10.m: Jamadagni was born by the power of austerity, the best of the knowers of brahman; / and the middle son was Śunaḥśepha, and Śunaḥpuccha was the youngest.

10.s:
viśvāmitraṃ tu dāyādaṃ gādhiḥ kuśikanandanaḥ
janayām āsa putraṃ tu tapovidyāśamātmakam //
10.d:
विश्वामित्रं तु दायादं गाधिः कुशिकनन्दनः
जनयाम् आस पुत्रं तु तपोविद्याशमात्मकम् ॥
10.m: And Gādhi, the son of Kuśika, fathered an heir, Viśvāmitra, / a son endowed with austerity, learning, and tranquility,

10.s:
prāpya brahmarṣisamatāṃ yo 'yaṃ brahmarṣitāṃ gataḥ
viśvāmitras tu dharmātmā nāmnā viśvarathaḥ smṛtaḥ //
10.d:
प्राप्य ब्रह्मर्षिसमतां यो ऽयं ब्रह्मर्षितां गतः
विश्वामित्रस् तु धर्मात्मा नाम्ना विश्वरथः स्मृतः ॥
10.m: who, having attained equality with the brahmanical sages, became a brahmanical sage. / Viśvāmitra was righteous-souled, known by the name Viśvaratha;

10.s:
jajñe bhṛguprasādena kauśikād vaṃśavardhanaḥ
viśvāmitrasya ca sutā devarātādayaḥ smṛtāḥ //
10.d:
जज्ञे भृगुप्रसादेन कौशिकाद् वंशवर्धनः
विश्वामित्रस्य च सुता देवरातादयः स्मृताः ॥
10.m: by the grace of Bhṛgu he was born from the descendant of Kuśika to increase the lineage. / And the sons of Viśvāmitra are remembered to begin with Devarāta,

10.s:
prakhyātās triṣu lokeṣu teṣāṃ nāmāny ataḥparam
devarātaḥ katiś caiva yasmāt kātyāyanāḥ smṛtāḥ //
10.d:
प्रख्यातास् त्रिषु लोकेषु तेषां नामान्य् अतःपरम्
देवरातः कतिश् चैव यस्मात् कात्यायनाः स्मृताः ॥
10.m: renowned in the three worlds. Hereafter are their names: / Devarāta, and Kati, from whom the Kātyāyanas are remembered;

10.s:
śālāvatyāṃ hiraṇyākṣo reṇur jajñe 'tha reṇukaḥ
sāṃkṛtir gālavaś caiva mudgalaś caiva viśrutaḥ //
10.d:
शालावत्यां हिरण्याक्षो रेणुर् जज्ञे ऽथ रेणुकः
सांकृतिर् गालवश् चैव मुद्गलश् चैव विश्रुतः ॥
10.m: upon Śālāvatī were born Hiraṇyākṣa, Reṇu, and Reṇuka, / Sāṃkṛti, Gālava, and the renowned Mudgala,

10.s:
madhucchando jayaś caiva devalaś ca tathāṣṭakaḥ
kacchapo hāritaś caiva viśvāmitrasya te sutāḥ //
10.d:
मधुच्छन्दो जयश् चैव देवलश् च तथाष्टकः
कच्छपो हारितश् चैव विश्वामित्रस्य ते सुताः ॥
10.m: Madhucchandas, Jaya, Devala, and Aṣṭaka, / Kacchapa, and Hārita—these were the sons of Viśvāmitra.

10.s:
teṣāṃ khyātāni gotrāṇi kauśikānāṃ mahātmanām
pāṇino babhravaś caiva dhyānajapyās tathaiva ca //
10.d:
तेषां ख्यातानि गोत्राणि कौशिकानां महात्मनाम्
पाणिनो बभ्रवश् चैव ध्यानजप्यास् तथैव च ॥
10.m: Famous are the gotras of these high-souled Kauśikas: / the Pāṇins, the Babhrus, and the Dhyānajapyas,

10.s:
pārthivā devarātāś ca śālaṅkāyanabāṣkalāḥ
lohitā yamadūtāś ca tathā kārūṣakāḥ smṛtāḥ //
10.d:
पार्थिवा देवराताश् च शालङ्कायनबाष्कलाः
लोहिता यमदूताश् च तथा कारूषकाः स्मृताः ॥
10.m: the Pārthivas, the Devarātas, the Śālaṅkāyanas and the Bāṣkalas, / the Lohitas, the Yamadūtas, and likewise the Kārūṣakas are remembered.

10.s:
pauravasya muniśreṣṭhā brahmarṣeḥ kauśikasya ca
saṃbandho 'py asya vaṃśe 'smin brahmakṣatrasya viśrutaḥ //
10.d:
पौरवस्य मुनिश्रेष्ठा ब्रह्मर्षेः कौशिकस्य च
संबन्धो ऽप्य् अस्य वंशे ऽस्मिन् ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य विश्रुतः ॥
10.m: O best of sages, the relationship between the descendant of Pūru and the brahmanical sage, the descendant of Kuśika, / in this lineage of both brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas is well known.

10.s:
viśvāmitrātmajānāṃ tu śunaḥśepho 'grajaḥ smṛtaḥ
bhārgavaḥ kauśikatvaṃ hi prāptaḥ sa munisattamaḥ //
10.d:
विश्वामित्रात्मजानां तु शुनःशेफो ऽग्रजः स्मृतः
भार्गवः कौशिकत्वं हि प्राप्तः स मुनिसत्तमः ॥
10.m: Among the sons of Viśvāmitra, Śunaḥśepha is remembered as the eldest; / for that best of sages, though born of Bhṛgu, attained the status of a Kauśika.

10.s:
viśvāmitrasya putras tu śunaḥśepho 'bhavat kila
haridaśvasya yajñe tu paśutve viniyojitaḥ //
10.d:
विश्वामित्रस्य पुत्रस् तु शुनःशेफो ऽभवत् किल
हरिदश्वस्य यज्ञे तु पशुत्वे विनियोजितः ॥
10.m: Śunaḥśepha indeed became the son of Viśvāmitra; / he had been appointed as the sacrificial animal at Haridaśva's sacrifice,

10.s:
devair dattaḥ śunaḥśepho viśvāmitrāya vai punaḥ
devair dattaḥ sa vai yasmād devarātas tato 'bhavat //
10.d:
देवैर् दत्तः शुनःशेफो विश्वामित्राय वै पुनः
देवैर् दत्तः स वै यस्माद् देवरातस् ततो ऽभवत् ॥
10.m: and Śunaḥśepha was given again to Viśvāmitra by the gods; / because he was given by the gods, he then became Devarāta.

10.s:
devarātādayaḥ sapta viśvāmitrasya vai sutāḥ
dṛṣadvatīsutaś cāpi vaiśvāmitras tathāṣṭakaḥ //
10.d:
देवरातादयः सप्त विश्वामित्रस्य वै सुताः
दृषद्वतीसुतश् चापि वैश्वामित्रस् तथाष्टकः ॥
10.m: The seven sons of Viśvāmitra begin with Devarāta; / and Aṣṭaka, the son of Viśvāmitra, was the son of Dṛṣadvatī.

10.s:
aṣṭakasya suto lauhiḥ prokto jahnugaṇo mayā
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vaṃśam āyor mahātmanaḥ //
10.d:
अष्टकस्य सुतो लौहिः प्रोक्तो जह्नुगणो मया
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वंशम् आयोर् महात्मनः ॥
10.m: The son of Aṣṭaka was Lauhi; the group of the Jahnu lineage has been related by me. / Hereafter I shall declare the lineage of the high-souled Āyu.

11.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
āyoḥ putrāś ca te pañca sarve vīrā mahārathāḥ
svarbhānutanayāyāṃ ca prabhāyāṃ jajñire nṛpāḥ //
11.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
आयोः पुत्राश् च ते पञ्च सर्वे वीरा महारथाः
स्वर्भानुतनयायां च प्रभायां जज्ञिरे नृपाः ॥
11.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / "The five sons of Āyu were all heroic, great chariot-warriors; / they were born as kings upon Prabhā, daughter of Svarbhānu.

11.s:
nahuṣaḥ prathamaṃ jajñe vṛddhaśarmā tataḥ param
rambho rajir anenāś ca triṣu lokeṣu viśrutāḥ //
11.d:
नहुषः प्रथमं जज्ञे वृद्धशर्मा ततः परम्
रम्भो रजिर् अनेनाश् च त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताः ॥
11.m: Nahuṣa was born first, and after him Vṛddhaśarman, / Rambha, Raji, and Anenas, renowned in the three worlds.

11.s:
rajiḥ putraśatānīha janayām āsa pañca vai
rājeyam iti vikhyātaṃ kṣatram indrabhayāvaham //
11.d:
रजिः पुत्रशतानीह जनयाम् आस पञ्च वै
राजेयम् इति विख्यातं क्षत्रम् इन्द्रभयावहम् ॥
11.m: Raji fathered here five hundred sons, / famous as the Rājeyas, a kṣatriya line that brought fear to Indra.

11.s:
yatra daivāsure yuddhe samutpanne sudāruṇe
devāś caivāsurāś caiva pitāmaham athābruvan //
11.d:
यत्र दैवासुरे युद्धे समुत्पन्ने सुदारुणे
देवाश् चैवासुराश् चैव पितामहम् अथाब्रुवन् ॥
11.m: When an exceedingly terrible war between the gods and asuras arose, / the gods and the asuras then spoke to the Grandfather [Brahmā]:

11.s:
devāsurā ūcuḥ
āvayor bhagavan yuddhe ko vijetā bhaviṣyati
brūhi naḥ sarvabhūteśa śrotum icchāma tattvataḥ //
11.d:
देवासुरा ऊचुः
आवयोर् भगवन् युद्धे को विजेता भविष्यति
ब्रूहि नः सर्वभूतेश श्रोतुम् इच्छाम तत्त्वतः ॥
11.m: The gods and asuras said: / 'O lord, who will be victorious in our battle? / Speak to us, O lord of all beings; we wish to hear the truth.'

11.s:
brahmovāca
yeṣām arthāya saṃgrāme rajir āttāyudhaḥ prabhuḥ
yotsyate te vijeṣyanti trīṃl lokān nātra saṃśayaḥ //
11.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
येषाम् अर्थाय संग्रामे रजिर् आत्तायुधः प्रभुः
योत्स्यते ते विजेष्यन्ति त्रींल् लोकान् नात्र संशयः ॥
11.m: Brahmā said: / 'Those for whose sake the powerful Raji fights in the battle with weapon raised, / they shall conquer the three worlds; of this there is no doubt.

11.s:
yato rajir dhṛtis tatra śrīś ca tatra yato dhṛtiḥ
yato dhṛtiś ca śrīś caiva dharmas tatra jayas tathā //
11.d:
यतो रजिर् धृतिस् तत्र श्रीश् च तत्र यतो धृतिः
यतो धृतिश् च श्रीश् चैव धर्मस् तत्र जयस् तथा ॥
11.m: Where Raji is, there is steadfastness; and where steadfastness is, there is prosperity; / where steadfastness and prosperity are, there is dharma and victory.'

11.s:
te devā dānavāḥ prītā devenoktā rajiṃ tadā
abhyayur jayam icchanto vṛṇvānās taṃ nararṣabham //
11.d:
ते देवा दानवाः प्रीता देवेनोक्ता रजिं तदा
अभ्ययुर् जयम् इच्छन्तो वृण्वानास् तं नरर्षभम् ॥
11.m: Those gods and dānavas, pleased when spoken to by the god, / then approached Raji, desiring victory and choosing that bull among men.

11.s:
sa hi svarbhānudauhitraḥ prabhāyāṃ samapadyata
rājā paramatejasvī somavaṃśavivardhanaḥ //
11.d:
स हि स्वर्भानुदौहित्रः प्रभायां समपद्यत
राजा परमतेजस्वी सोमवंशविवर्धनः ॥
11.m: For he was born as the daughter's son of Svarbhānu through Prabhā, / a king of supreme splendor, increaser of the Lunar dynasty.

11.s:
te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve rajiṃ vai devadānavāḥ
ūcur asmajjayāya tvaṃ gṛhāṇa varakārmukam //
11.d:
ते हृष्टमनसः सर्वे रजिं वै देवदानवाः
ऊचुर् अस्मज्जयाय त्वं गृहाण वरकार्मुकम् ॥
11.m: All those gods and Dānavas, glad at heart, / said to Raji: "Take up the supreme bow for our victory!"

11.s:
athovāca rajis tatra tayor vai devadaityayoḥ
arthajñaḥ svārtham uddiśya yaśaḥ svaṃ ca prakāśayan //
11.d:
अथोवाच रजिस् तत्र तयोर् वै देवदैत्ययोः
अर्थज्ञः स्वार्थम् उद्दिश्य यशः स्वं च प्रकाशयन् ॥
11.m: Then Raji, knowing what was expedient, declared his own purpose / and, proclaiming his own renown, said to both the gods and Daityas:

11.s:
rajir uvāca
yadi daityagaṇān sarvāñ jitvā vīryeṇa vāsavaḥ
indro bhavāmi dharmeṇa tato yotsyāmi saṃyuge //
11.d:
रजिर् उवाच
यदि दैत्यगणान् सर्वाञ् जित्वा वीर्येण वासवः
इन्द्रो भवामि धर्मेण ततो योत्स्यामि संयुगे ॥
11.m: Raji said: / "If, having conquered all the hosts of Daityas by my valor, / I rightfully become Indra, the Vāsava, then I will fight in battle."

11.s:
devāḥ prathamato viprāḥ pratīyur hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
evaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ nṛpate kāmaḥ saṃpadyatāṃ tava //
11.d:
देवाः प्रथमतो विप्राः प्रतीयुर् हृष्टमानसाः
एवं यथेष्टं नृपते कामः संपद्यतां तव ॥
11.m: The gods, O twice-born ones, agreed at once with glad minds: / "So be it, O king, as you desire! Let your wish be fulfilled!"

11.s:
śrutvā suragaṇānāṃ tu vākyaṃ rājā rajis tadā
papracchāsuramukhyāṃs tu yathā devān apṛcchata //
11.d:
श्रुत्वा सुरगणानां तु वाक्यं राजा रजिस् तदा
पप्रच्छासुरमुख्यांस् तु यथा देवान् अपृच्छत ॥
11.m: Hearing the word of the hosts of gods, King Raji then / questioned the leaders of the Asuras just as he had questioned the gods.

11.s:
dānavā darpasaṃpūrṇāḥ svārtham evāvagamya ha
pratyūcus taṃ nṛpavaraṃ sābhimānam idaṃ vacaḥ //
11.d:
दानवा दर्पसंपूर्णाः स्वार्थम् एवावगम्य ह
प्रत्यूचुस् तं नृपवरं साभिमानम् इदं वचः ॥
11.m: The Dānavas, filled with pride and mindful only of their own interest, / gave that best of kings this haughty reply:

11.s:
dānavā ūcuḥ
asmākam indraḥ prahrādo yasyārthe vijayāmahe
asmiṃs tu samare rājaṃs tiṣṭha tvaṃ rājasattama //
11.d:
दानवा ऊचुः
अस्माकम् इन्द्रः प्रह्रादो यस्यार्थे विजयामहे
अस्मिंस् तु समरे राजंस् तिष्ठ त्वं राजसत्तम ॥
11.m: The Dānavas said: / "Our Indra is Prahrāda, for whose sake we conquer. / But in this battle, O king, O best of kings, do you stand aside!"

11.s:
sa tatheti bruvann eva devair apy aticoditaḥ
bhaviṣyasīndro jitvainaṃ devair uktas tu pārthivaḥ //
11.d:
स तथेति ब्रुवन्न् एव देवैर् अप्य् अतिचोदितः
भविष्यसीन्द्रो जित्वैनं देवैर् उक्तस् तु पार्थिवः ॥
11.m: Saying "So be it," strongly urged by the gods, / the king was told by the gods: "You will become Indra after conquering them!"

11.s:
jaghāna dānavān sarvān ye 'vadhyā vajrapāṇinaḥ
sa vipranaṣṭāṃ devānāṃ paramaśrīḥ śriyaṃ vaśī //
11.d:
जघान दानवान् सर्वान् ये ऽवध्या वज्रपाणिनः
स विप्रनष्टां देवानां परमश्रीः श्रियं वशी ॥
11.m: Possessed of supreme splendor and self-control, he struck down all the Dānavas / who could not be slain by the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the lost fortune of the gods

11.s:
nihatya dānavān sarvān ājahāra rajiḥ prabhuḥ
tato rajiṃ mahāvīryaṃ devaiḥ saha śatakratuḥ //
11.d:
निहत्य दानवान् सर्वान् आजहार रजिः प्रभुः
ततो रजिं महावीर्यं देवैः सह शतक्रतुः ॥
11.m: Lord Raji restored, having slain all the Dānavas. / Then Śatakratu, along with the gods, [approaching] the mighty Raji,

11.s:
rajiputro 'ham ity uktvā punar evābravīd vacaḥ
indro 'si tāta devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ //
11.d:
रजिपुत्रो ऽहम् इत्य् उक्त्वा पुनर् एवाब्रवीद् वचः
इन्द्रो ऽसि तात देवानां सर्वेषां नात्र संशयः ॥
11.m: said: "I am Raji's son!" and spoke this word again: / "Father, you are Indra over all the gods; there is no doubt about this.

11.s:
yasyāham indraḥ putras te khyātiṃ yāsyāmi karmabhiḥ
sa tu śakravacaḥ śrutvā vañcitas tena māyayā //
11.d:
यस्याहम् इन्द्रः पुत्रस् ते ख्यातिं यास्यामि कर्मभिः
स तु शक्रवचः श्रुत्वा वञ्चितस् तेन मायया ॥
11.m: I, whose father is Indra, shall attain fame through your deeds." / Hearing Śakra's words, he was deceived by his trickery,

11.s:
tathaivety abravīd rājā prīyamāṇaḥ śatakratum
tasmiṃs tu devaiḥ sadṛśo divaṃ prāpte mahīpatau //
11.d:
तथैवेत्य् अब्रवीद् राजा प्रीयमाणः शतक्रतुम्
तस्मिंस् तु देवैः सदृशो दिवं प्राप्ते महीपतौ ॥
11.m: and the pleased king said to Śatakratu: "So be it." / But when that king, equal to the gods, went to heaven,

11.s:
dāyādyam indrād ājahrū rājyaṃ tattanayā rajeḥ
pañca putraśatāny asya tad vai sthānaṃ śatakratoḥ //
11.d:
दायाद्यम् इन्द्राद् आजह्रू राज्यं तत्तनया रजेः
पञ्च पुत्रशतान्य् अस्य तद् वै स्थानं शतक्रतोः ॥
11.m: the sons of Raji wrested the inheritance and the kingdom from Indra; / his five hundred sons seized that very realm of Śatakratu,

11.s:
samākrāmanta bahudhā svargalokaṃ triviṣṭapam
te yadā tu svasaṃmūḍhā rāgonmattā vidharmiṇaḥ //
11.d:
समाक्रामन्त बहुधा स्वर्गलोकं त्रिविष्टपम्
ते यदा तु स्वसंमूढा रागोन्मत्ता विधर्मिणः ॥
11.m: and they overran the heaven world, the Triviṣṭapa, on every side. / But when they became infatuated, blinded by passion, devoid of dharma,

11.s:
brahmadviṣaś ca saṃvṛttā hatavīryaparākramāḥ
tato lebhe svam aiśvaryam indraḥ sthānaṃ tathottamam //
11.d:
ब्रह्मद्विषश् च संवृत्ता हतवीर्यपराक्रमाः
ततो लेभे स्वम् ऐश्वर्यम् इन्द्रः स्थानं तथोत्तमम् ॥
11.m: and haters of brāhmaṇas, their strength and prowess destroyed, / Indra then recovered his sovereignty and supreme position

11.s:
hatvā rajisutān sarvān kāmakrodhaparāyaṇān
ya idaṃ cyāvanaṃ sthānāt pratiṣṭhānaṃ śatakratoḥ
śṛṇuyād dhārayed vāpi na sa daurgatyam āpnuyāt //
11.d:
हत्वा रजिसुतान् सर्वान् कामक्रोधपरायणान्
य इदं च्यावनं स्थानात् प्रतिष्ठानं शतक्रतोः
शृणुयाद् धारयेद् वापि न स दौर्गत्यम् आप्नुयात् ॥
11.m: by slaying all of Raji's sons, who were given over to lust and wrath. / Whoever hears or retains this expulsion from his realm and the reinstatement of Śatakratu / shall never suffer misfortune.

11.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
rambho 'napatyas tv āsīc ca vaṃśaṃ vakṣyāmy anenasaḥ
anenasaḥ suto rājā pratikṣatro mahāyaśāḥ //
11.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
रम्भो ऽनपत्यस् त्व् आसीच् च वंशं वक्ष्याम्य् अनेनसः
अनेनसः सुतो राजा प्रतिक्षत्रो महायशाः ॥
11.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Rambha was childless. I shall now declare the lineage of Anenas: / the son of Anenas was the renowned king Pratikṣatra.

11.s:
pratikṣatrasutaś cāsīt saṃjayo nāma viśrutaḥ
saṃjayasya jayaḥ putro vijayas tasya cātmajaḥ //
11.d:
प्रतिक्षत्रसुतश् चासीत् संजयो नाम विश्रुतः
संजयस्य जयः पुत्रो विजयस् तस्य चात्मजः ॥
11.m: The son of Pratikṣatra was famous by the name Saṃjaya; / Saṃjaya's son was Jaya, and his son was Vijaya.

11.s:
vijayasya kṛtiḥ putras tasya haryatvataḥ sutaḥ
haryatvatasuto rājā sahadevaḥ pratāpavān //
11.d:
विजयस्य कृतिः पुत्रस् तस्य हर्यत्वतः सुतः
हर्यत्वतसुतो राजा सहदेवः प्रतापवान् ॥
11.m: Vijaya's son was Kṛti, and his son was Haryatvata; / the son of Haryatvata was the glorious king Sahadeva.

11.s:
sahadevasya dharmātmā nadīna iti viśrutaḥ
nadīnasya jayatseno jayatsenasya saṃkṛtiḥ //
11.d:
सहदेवस्य धर्मात्मा नदीन इति विश्रुतः
नदीनस्य जयत्सेनो जयत्सेनस्य संकृतिः ॥
11.m: The son of Sahadeva was the righteous one celebrated as Nadīna; / Nadīna's [son] was Jayatsena, and Jayatsena's was Saṃkṛti.

11.s:
saṃkṛter api dharmātmā kṣatravṛddho mahāyaśāḥ
anenasaḥ samākhyātāḥ kṣatravṛddhasya cāparaḥ //
11.d:
संकृतेर् अपि धर्मात्मा क्षत्रवृद्धो महायशाः
अनेनसः समाख्याताः क्षत्रवृद्धस्य चापरः ॥
11.m: From Saṃkṛti was born the righteous and highly renowned Kṣatravṛddha. / These descendants of Anenas have been recounted, and next is Kṣatravṛddha's.

11.s:
kṣatravṛddhātmajas tatra sunahotro mahāyaśāḥ
sunahotrasya dāyādās trayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ //
11.d:
क्षत्रवृद्धात्मजस् तत्र सुनहोत्रो महायशाः
सुनहोत्रस्य दायादास् त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः ॥
11.m: The son of Kṣatravṛddha was the famous Sunahotra; / Sunahotra had three most righteous heirs:

11.s:
kāśaḥ śalaś ca dvāv etau tathā gṛtsamadaḥ prabhuḥ
putro gṛtsamadasyāpi śunako yasya śaunakaḥ //
11.d:
काशः शलश् च द्वाव् एतौ तथा गृत्समदः प्रभुः
पुत्रो गृत्समदस्यापि शुनको यस्य शौनकः ॥
11.m: these two, Kāśa and Śala, and also the lord Gṛtsamada; / the son of Gṛtsamada was Śunaka, whose [son was] Śaunaka.

11.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāś caiva vaiśyāḥ śūdrās tathaiva ca
śalātmaja ārṣṭiseṇas tanayas tasya kāśyapaḥ //
11.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाश् चैव वैश्याः शूद्रास् तथैव च
शलात्मज आर्ष्टिसेणस् तनयस् तस्य काश्यपः ॥
11.m: [From him arose] brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras. / Śala's son was Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, and his son was Kāśyapa.

11.s:
kāśasya kāśipo rājā putro dīrghatapās tathā
dhanus tu dīrghatapaso vidvān dhanvantaris tataḥ //
11.d:
काशस्य काशिपो राजा पुत्रो दीर्घतपास् तथा
धनुस् तु दीर्घतपसो विद्वान् धन्वन्तरिस् ततः ॥
11.m: Kāśa's [son] was King Kāśipa, and his son was Dīrghatapas; / Dīrghatapas's son was Dhanu, and from him arose the learned Dhanvantari.

11.s:
tapaso 'nte sumahato jāto vṛddhasya dhīmataḥ
punar dhanvantarir devo mānuṣeṣv iha janmani //
11.d:
तपसो ऽन्ते सुमहतो जातो वृद्धस्य धीमतः
पुनर् धन्वन्तरिर् देवो मानुषेष्व् इह जन्मनि ॥
11.m: At the conclusion of immense ascetic heat, the divine Dhanvantari was born / to that wise old man, appearing again among mortals in this birth.

11.s:
tasya gehe samutpanno devo dhanvantaris tadā
kāśirājo mahārājaḥ sarvarogapraṇāśanaḥ //
11.d:
तस्य गेहे समुत्पन्नो देवो धन्वन्तरिस् तदा
काशिराजो महाराजः सर्वरोगप्रणाशनः ॥
11.m: Then in his house was born the god Dhanvantari, / the king of Kāśī, a great king who destroys all diseases.

11.s:
āyurvedaṃ bharadvājāt prāpyeha sa bhiṣakkriyaḥ
tam aṣṭadhā punar vyasya śiṣyebhyaḥ pratyapādayat //
11.d:
आयुर्वेदं भरद्वाजात् प्राप्येह स भिषक्क्रियः
तम् अष्टधा पुनर् व्यस्य शिष्येभ्यः प्रत्यपादयत् ॥
11.m: Having received Ayurveda here from Bharadvāja, he practiced medicine; / dividing it again into eight parts, he taught it to his disciples.

11.s:
dhanvantares tu tanayaḥ ketumān iti viśrutaḥ
atha ketumataḥ putro vīro bhīmarathaḥ smṛtaḥ //
11.d:
धन्वन्तरेस् तु तनयः केतुमान् इति विश्रुतः
अथ केतुमतः पुत्रो वीरो भीमरथः स्मृतः ॥
11.m: Dhanvantari's son was celebrated as Ketumant; / and Ketumant's son is remembered as the heroic Bhīmaratha.

11.s:
putro bhīmarathasyāpi divodāsaḥ prajeśvaraḥ
divodāsas tu dharmātmā vārāṇasyadhipo 'bhavat //
11.d:
पुत्रो भीमरथस्यापि दिवोदासः प्रजेश्वरः
दिवोदासस् तु धर्मात्मा वाराणस्यधिपो ऽभवत् ॥
11.m: The son of Bhīmaratha was Divodāsa, lord of subjects; / and the righteous Divodāsa became the ruler of Vārāṇasī.

11.s:
etasminn eva kāle tu purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ dvijāḥ
śūnyāṃ niveśayām āsa kṣemako nāma rākṣasaḥ //
11.d:
एतस्मिन्न् एव काले तु पुरीं वाराणसीं द्विजाः
शून्यां निवेशयाम् आस क्षेमको नाम राक्षसः ॥
11.m: At that very time, O twice-born ones, a rākṣasa named Kṣemaka / settled the desolate city of Vārāṇasī.

11.s:
śaptā hi sā matimatā nikumbhena mahātmanā
śūnyā varṣasahasraṃ vai bhavitrī tu na saṃśayaḥ //
11.d:
शप्ता हि सा मतिमता निकुम्भेन महात्मना
शून्या वर्षसहस्रं वै भवित्री तु न संशयः ॥
11.m: For it had been cursed by the wise and great-souled Nikumbha: / "It shall surely be desolate for a thousand years; there is no doubt."

11.s:
tasyāṃ hi śaptamātrāyāṃ divodāsaḥ prajeśvaraḥ
viṣayānte purīṃ ramyāṃ gomatyāṃ saṃnyaveśayat //
11.d:
तस्यां हि शप्तमात्रायां दिवोदासः प्रजेश्वरः
विषयान्ते पुरीं रम्यां गोमत्यां संन्यवेशयत् ॥
11.m: As soon as it was cursed, Divodāsa, the lord of subjects, / founded a delightful city on the border of his realm along the Gomatī.

11.s:
bhadraśreṇyasya pūrvaṃ tu purī vārāṇasī abhūt
bhadraśreṇyasya putrāṇāṃ śatam uttamadhanvinām //
11.d:
भद्रश्रेण्यस्य पूर्वं तु पुरी वाराणसी अभूत्
भद्रश्रेण्यस्य पुत्राणां शतम् उत्तमधन्विनाम् ॥
11.m: The city of Vārāṇasī had previously belonged to Bhadraśreṇya; / slaying the hundred sons of Bhadraśreṇya, excellent archers,

11.s:
hatvā niveśayām āsa divodāso narādhipaḥ
bhadraśreṇyasya tad rājyaṃ hṛtaṃ yena balīyasā //
11.d:
हत्वा निवेशयाम् आस दिवोदासो नराधिपः
भद्रश्रेण्यस्य तद् राज्यं हृतं येन बलीयसा ॥
11.m: King Divodāsa occupied it; / by him, the more powerful one, the kingdom of Bhadraśreṇya was seized.

11.s:
bhadraśreṇyasya putras tu durdamo nāma viśrutaḥ
divodāsena bāleti ghṛṇayā sa visarjitaḥ //
11.d:
भद्रश्रेण्यस्य पुत्रस् तु दुर्दमो नाम विश्रुतः
दिवोदासेन बालेति घृणया स विसर्जितः ॥
11.m: A son of Bhadraśreṇya was famous as Durdama; / he was spared by Divodāsa out of pity because he was a child.

11.s:
haihayasya tu dāyādyaṃ hṛtavān vai mahīpatiḥ
ājahre pitṛdāyādyaṃ divodāsahṛtaṃ balāt //
11.d:
हैहयस्य तु दायाद्यं हृतवान् वै महीपतिः
आजह्रे पितृदायाद्यं दिवोदासहृतं बलात् ॥
11.m: That king seized the inheritance of the Haihaya; / he forcibly recovered his ancestral inheritance which had been taken by Divodāsa.

11.s:
bhadraśreṇyasya putreṇa durdamena mahātmanā
vairasyānto mahābhāgāḥ kṛtaś cātmīyatejasā //
11.d:
भद्रश्रेण्यस्य पुत्रेण दुर्दमेन महात्मना
वैरस्यान्तो महाभागाः कृतश् चात्मीयतेजसा ॥
11.m: By Durdama, the great-souled son of Bhadraśreṇya, / an end to the enmity was brought about by his own valor, O fortunate ones.

11.s:
divodāsād dṛṣadvatyāṃ vīro jajñe pratardanaḥ
tena bālena putreṇa prahṛtaṃ tu punar balam //
11.d:
दिवोदासाद् दृषद्वत्यां वीरो जज्ञे प्रतर्दनः
तेन बालेन पुत्रेण प्रहृतं तु पुनर् बलम् ॥
11.m: From Divodāsa, the hero Pratardana was born to Dṛṣadvatī; / by that son, while still a boy, his army was struck back again.

11.s:
pratardanasya putrau dvau vatsabhargau suviśrutau
vatsaputro hy alarkas tu saṃnatis tasya cātmajaḥ //
11.d:
प्रतर्दनस्य पुत्रौ द्वौ वत्सभर्गौ सुविश्रुतौ
वत्सपुत्रो ह्य् अलर्कस् तु संनतिस् तस्य चात्मजः ॥
11.m: Pratardana had two renowned sons, Vatsa and Bharga; / Vatsa's son was Alarka, and Saṃnati was his son.

11.s:
alarkas tasya putras tu brahmaṇyaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
alarkaṃ prati rājarṣiṃ śloko gītaḥ purātanaiḥ //
11.d:
अलर्कस् तस्य पुत्रस् तु ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यसंगरः
अलर्कं प्रति राजर्षिं श्लोको गीतः पुरातनैः ॥
11.m: Alarka was his son, devoted to brāhmaṇas and true to his vows; / concerning the royal sage Alarka, a verse was sung by the ancients:

11.s:
ṣaṣṭir varṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭir varṣaśatāni ca
yuvā rūpeṇa saṃpannaḥ prāg āsīc ca kulodvahaḥ //
11.d:
षष्टिर् वर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिर् वर्षशतानि च
युवा रूपेण संपन्नः प्राग् आसीच् च कुलोद्वहः ॥
11.m: "For sixty thousand years and sixty hundred years, / this uplifter of his race was youthful and possessed of beauty."

11.s:
lopāmudrāprasādena paramāyur avāptavān
tasyāsīt sumahad rājyaṃ rūpayauvanaśālinaḥ //
11.d:
लोपामुद्राप्रसादेन परमायुर् अवाप्तवान्
तस्यासीत् सुमहद् राज्यं रूपयौवनशालिनः ॥
11.m: By the favor of Lopāmudrā he attained supreme longevity; / he who possessed beauty and youth held a very vast kingdom.

11.s:
śāpasyānte mahābāhur hatvā kṣemakarākṣasam
ramyāṃ niveśayām āsa purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ punaḥ //
11.d:
शापस्यान्ते महाबाहुर् हत्वा क्षेमकराक्षसम्
रम्यां निवेशयाम् आस पुरीं वाराणसीं पुनः ॥
11.m: At the end of the curse, the mighty-armed one, having slain the rākṣasa Kṣemaka, / resettled the delightful city of Vārāṇasī once more.

11.s:
saṃnater api dāyādaḥ sunītho nāma dhārmikaḥ
sunīthasya tu dāyādaḥ kṣemo nāma mahāyaśāḥ //
11.d:
संनतेर् अपि दायादः सुनीथो नाम धार्मिकः
सुनीथस्य तु दायादः क्षेमो नाम महायशाः ॥
11.m: Saṃnati's heir was the righteous one named Sunītha; / and Sunītha's heir was the highly renowned Kṣema.

11.s:
kṣemasya ketumān putraḥ suketus tasya cātmajaḥ
suketos tanayaś cāpi dharmaketur iti smṛtaḥ //
11.d:
क्षेमस्य केतुमान् पुत्रः सुकेतुस् तस्य चात्मजः
सुकेतोस् तनयश् चापि धर्मकेतुर् इति स्मृतः ॥
11.m: Kṣema's son was Ketumān, and Suketu was his son; / and the son of Suketu was known as Dharmaketu.

11.s:
dharmaketos tu dāyādaḥ satyaketur mahārathaḥ
satyaketusutaś cāpi vibhur nāma prajeśvaraḥ //
11.d:
धर्मकेतोस् तु दायादः सत्यकेतुर् महारथः
सत्यकेतुसुतश् चापि विभुर् नाम प्रजेश्वरः ॥
11.m: Dharmaketu's heir was the great car-warrior Satyaketu; / and Satyaketu's son was Vibhu, lord of subjects.

11.s:
ānartas tu vibhoḥ putraḥ sukumāraś ca tatsutaḥ
sukumārasya putras tu dhṛṣṭaketuḥ sudhārmikaḥ //
11.d:
आनर्तस् तु विभोः पुत्रः सुकुमारश् च तत्सुतः
सुकुमारस्य पुत्रस् तु धृष्टकेतुः सुधार्मिकः ॥
11.m: Ānarta was the son of Vibhu, and Sukumāra was his son; / Sukumāra's son was the exceedingly righteous Dhṛṣṭaketu.

11.s:
dhṛṣṭaketos tu dāyādo veṇuhotraḥ prajeśvaraḥ
veṇuhotrasutaś cāpi bhārgo nāma prajeśvaraḥ //
11.d:
धृष्टकेतोस् तु दायादो वेणुहोत्रः प्रजेश्वरः
वेणुहोत्रसुतश् चापि भार्गो नाम प्रजेश्वरः ॥
11.m: Dhṛṣṭaketu's heir was Veṇuhotra, lord of subjects; / and Veṇuhotra's son was the lord of subjects named Bhārga.

11.s:
vatsasya vatsabhūmis tu bhārgabhūmis tu bhārgajaḥ
ete tv aṅgirasaḥ putrā jātā vaṃśe 'tha bhārgava //
11.d:
वत्सस्य वत्सभूमिस् तु भार्गभूमिस् तु भार्गजः
एते त्व् अङ्गिरसः पुत्रा जाता वंशे ऽथ भार्गव ॥
11.m: From Vatsa came Vatsabhūmi, and from Bhārga came Bhārgabhūmi. / These sons of Aṅgiras, O descendant of Bhṛgu, were born in this lineage.

11.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyās trayaḥ putrāḥ sahasraśaḥ
ity ete kāśyapāḥ proktā nahuṣasya nibodhata //
11.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्यास् त्रयः पुत्राः सहस्रशः
इत्य् एते काश्यपाः प्रोक्ता नहुषस्य निबोधत ॥
11.m: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas—[their] sons were three in thousands. / Thus have these descendants of Kāśya been described; now hear of Nahuṣa.

12.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
utpannāḥ pitṛkanyāyāṃ virajāyāṃ mahaujasaḥ
nahuṣasya tu dāyādāḥ ṣaḍ indropamatejasaḥ //
12.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
उत्पन्नाः पितृकन्यायां विरजायां महौजसः
नहुषस्य तु दायादाः षड् इन्द्रोपमतेजसः ॥
12.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Born from the daughters of the Pitṛs, the pure Virajā, / Nahuṣa had six heirs of great power, equal in splendour to Indra:

12.s:
yatir yayātiḥ saṃyātir āyātiḥ pārśvako 'bhavat
yatir jyeṣṭhas tu teṣāṃ vai yayātis tu tataḥ param //
12.d:
यतिर् ययातिः संयातिर् आयातिः पार्श्वको ऽभवत्
यतिर् ज्येष्ठस् तु तेषां वै ययातिस् तु ततः परम् ॥
12.m: Yati, Yayāti, Saṃyāti, Āyāti, and Pārśvaka arose. / Yati was indeed the eldest among them, and after him Yayāti.

12.s:
kakutsthakanyāṃ gāṃ nāma lebhe paramadhārmikaḥ
yatis tu mokṣam āsthāya brahmabhūto 'bhavan muniḥ //
12.d:
ककुत्स्थकन्यां गां नाम लेभे परमधार्मिकः
यतिस् तु मोक्षम् आस्थाय ब्रह्मभूतो ऽभवन् मुनिः ॥
12.m: The supremely righteous one took as wife Gā, the daughter of Kakutstha. / But Yati, taking refuge in liberation, became a sage absorbed in brahman.

12.s:
teṣāṃ yayātiḥ pañcānāṃ vijitya vasudhām imām
devayānīm uśanasaḥ sutāṃ bhāryām avāpa saḥ //
12.d:
तेषां ययातिः पञ्चानां विजित्य वसुधाम् इमाम्
देवयानीम् उशनसः सुतां भार्याम् अवाप सः ॥
12.m: Among those five, Yayāti, having conquered this earth, / obtained as his wife Devayānī, the daughter of Uśanas,

12.s:
śarmiṣṭhām āsurīṃ caiva tanayāṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata //
12.d:
शर्मिष्ठाम् आसुरीं चैव तनयां वृषपर्वणः
यदुं च तुर्वसुं चैव देवयानी व्यजायत ॥
12.m: and also the Asura maiden Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. / Devayānī gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu;

12.s:
druhyaṃ cānuṃ ca puruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī
tasmai śakro dadau prīto rathaṃ paramabhāsvaram //
12.d:
द्रुह्यं चानुं च पुरुं च शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी
तस्मै शक्रो ददौ प्रीतो रथं परमभास्वरम् ॥
12.m: and Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, to Druhyu, Anu, and Puru. / Well-pleased, Śakra gave to him a supremely radiant chariot,

12.s:
aṅgadaṃ kāñcanaṃ divyaṃ divyaiḥ paramavājibhiḥ
yuktaṃ manojavaiḥ śubhrair yena kāryaṃ samudvahan //
12.d:
अङ्गदं काञ्चनं दिव्यं दिव्यैः परमवाजिभिः
युक्तं मनोजवैः शुभ्रैर् येन कार्यं समुद्वहन् ॥
12.m: provided with armlets, golden, divine, yoked with divine, supreme steeds / that were white and as swift as thought, by means of which, accomplishing his deeds,

12.s:
sa tena rathamukhyena ṣaḍrātreṇājayan mahīm
yayātir yudhi durdharṣas tathā devān sadānavān //
12.d:
स तेन रथमुख्येन षड्रात्रेणाजयन् महीम्
ययातिर् युधि दुर्धर्षस् तथा देवान् सदानवान् ॥
12.m: Yayāti, invincible in battle, conquered the earth in six nights / by means of that foremost chariot, and likewise conquered the gods together with the Dānavas.

12.s:
sarathaḥ kauravāṇāṃ tu sarveṣām abhavat tadā
saṃvartavasunāmnas tu kauravāj janamejayāt //
12.d:
सरथः कौरवाणां तु सर्वेषाम् अभवत् तदा
संवर्तवसुनाम्नस् तु कौरवाज् जनमेजयात् ॥
12.m: That chariot then belonged to all the Kauravas, / until from the Kaurava Janamejaya, named Saṃvartavasu,

12.s:
kuroḥ putrasya rājendrarājñaḥ pārīkṣitasya ha
jagāma sa ratho nāśaṃ śāpād gargasya dhīmataḥ //
12.d:
कुरोः पुत्रस्य राजेन्द्रराज्ञः पारीक्षितस्य ह
जगाम स रथो नाशं शापाद् गर्गस्य धीमतः ॥
12.m: the son of Kuru, the king of kings and descendant of Parīkṣit, / that chariot went to destruction through the curse of the wise Garga.

12.s:
gargasya hi sutaṃ bālaṃ sa rājā janamejayaḥ
kālena hiṃsayām āsa brahmahatyām avāpa saḥ //
12.d:
गर्गस्य हि सुतं बालं स राजा जनमेजयः
कालेन हिंसयाम् आस ब्रह्महत्याम् अवाप सः ॥
12.m: For in the course of time King Janamejaya killed / the young child of Garga, and he incurred the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa.

12.s:
sa lohagandhī rājarṣiḥ paridhāvann itas tataḥ
paurajānapadais tyakto na lebhe śarma karhicit //
12.d:
स लोहगन्धी राजर्षिः परिधावन्न् इतस् ततः
पौरजानपदैस् त्यक्तो न लेभे शर्म कर्हिचित् ॥
12.m: Smelling of raw iron, the royal sage wandered here and there; / abandoned by the citizens and countryfolk, he found no peace anywhere.

12.s:
tataḥ sa duḥkhasaṃtapto nālabhat saṃvidaṃ kvacit
viprendraṃ śaunakaṃ rājā śaraṇaṃ pratyapadyata //
12.d:
ततः स दुःखसंतप्तो नालभत् संविदं क्वचित्
विप्रेन्द्रं शौनकं राजा शरणं प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
12.m: Then, burning with sorrow and finding no relief anywhere, / the king went for refuge to the foremost vipra, Śaunaka.

12.s:
yājayām āsa ca jñānī śaunako janamejayam
aśvamedhena rājānaṃ pāvanārthaṃ dvijottamāḥ //
12.d:
याजयाम् आस च ज्ञानी शौनको जनमेजयम्
अश्वमेधेन राजानं पावनार्थं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
12.m: And the wise Śaunaka made King Janamejaya perform / the horse sacrifice for purification, O best of twice-borns.

12.s:
sa lohagandho vyanaśat tasyāvabhṛtham etya ca
sa ca divyaratho rājño vaśaś cedipates tadā //
12.d:
स लोहगन्धो व्यनशत् तस्यावभृथम् एत्य च
स च दिव्यरथो राज्ञो वशश् चेदिपतेस् तदा ॥
12.m: When he reached the concluding bath of that [sacrifice], that stench of raw iron vanished, / and that divine chariot then came under the control of the king of Cedi.

12.s:
dattaḥ śakreṇa tuṣṭena lebhe tasmād bṛhadrathaḥ
bṛhadrathāt krameṇaiva gato bārhadrathaṃ nṛpam //
12.d:
दत्तः शक्रेण तुष्टेन लेभे तस्माद् बृहद्रथः
बृहद्रथात् क्रमेणैव गतो बार्हद्रथं नृपम् ॥
12.m: Given by Śakra, who was pleased, Bṛhadratha received it from him; / from Bṛhadratha it went in succession to the king born of Bṛhadratha.

12.s:
tato hatvā jarāsaṃdhaṃ bhīmas taṃ ratham uttamam
pradadau vāsudevāya prītyā kauravanandanaḥ //
12.d:
ततो हत्वा जरासंधं भीमस् तं रथम् उत्तमम्
प्रददौ वासुदेवाय प्रीत्या कौरवनन्दनः ॥
12.m: Then, having slain Jarāsaṃdha, Bhīma, the delight of the Kurus, / gave that best chariot with affection to Vāsudeva.

12.s:
saptadvīpāṃ yayātis tu jitvā pṛthvīṃ sasāgarām
vibhajya pañcadhā rājyaṃ putrāṇāṃ nāhuṣas tadā //
12.d:
सप्तद्वीपां ययातिस् तु जित्वा पृथ्वीं ससागराम्
विभज्य पञ्चधा राज्यं पुत्राणां नाहुषस् तदा ॥
12.m: Then Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, having conquered the seven-islanded earth / along with the oceans, divided the kingdom fivefold among his sons.

12.s:
yayātir diśi pūrvasyāṃ yaduṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ nyayojayat
madhye puruṃ ca rājānam abhyaṣiñcat sa nāhuṣaḥ //
12.d:
ययातिर् दिशि पूर्वस्यां यदुं ज्येष्ठं न्ययोजयत्
मध्ये पुरुं च राजानम् अभ्यषिञ्चत् स नाहुषः ॥
12.m: Yayāti assigned the eldest, Yadu, to the eastern quarter, / and that son of Nahuṣa consecrated Puru as king in the center;

12.s:
diśi dakṣiṇapūrvasyāṃ turvasuṃ matimān nṛpaḥ
tair iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā //
12.d:
दिशि दक्षिणपूर्वस्यां तुर्वसुं मतिमान् नृपः
तैर् इयं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना ॥
12.m: the wise king [assigned] Turvasu to the south-eastern quarter. / By them this whole earth with its seven islands and cities,

12.s:
yathāpradeśam adyāpi dharmeṇa pratipālyate
prajās teṣāṃ purastāt tu vakṣyāmi munisattamāḥ //
12.d:
यथाप्रदेशम् अद्यापि धर्मेण प्रतिपाल्यते
प्रजास् तेषां पुरस्तात् तु वक्ष्यामि मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
12.m: according to each region, is protected in accordance with dharma even today. / I shall speak of their offspring hereafter, O best of sages.

12.s:
dhanur nyasya pṛṣatkāṃś ca pañcabhiḥ puruṣarṣabhaiḥ
jarāvān abhavad rājā bhāram āveśya bandhuṣu //
12.d:
धनुर् न्यस्य पृषत्कांश् च पञ्चभिः पुरुषर्षभैः
जरावान् अभवद् राजा भारम् आवेश्य बन्धुषु ॥
12.m: Having laid down his bow and arrows along with those five bulls among men, / the king grew old, transferring the burden [of state] to his kinsmen.

12.s:
nikṣiptaśastraḥ pṛthivīṃ cacāra pṛthivīpatiḥ
prītimān abhavad rājā yayātir aparājitaḥ //
12.d:
निक्षिप्तशस्त्रः पृथिवीं चचार पृथिवीपतिः
प्रीतिमान् अभवद् राजा ययातिर् अपराजितः ॥
12.m: Laying aside his weapons, the lord of the earth traversed the earth; / the undefeated King Yayāti was full of delight.

12.s:
evaṃ vibhajya pṛthivīṃ yayātir yadum abravīt
jarāṃ me pratigṛhṇīṣva putra kṛtyāntareṇa vai //
12.d:
एवं विभज्य पृथिवीं ययातिर् यदुम् अब्रवीत्
जरां मे प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्र कृत्यान्तरेण वै ॥
12.m: Having thus divided the earth, Yayāti said to Yadu: / 'Take my old age, my son, for the purpose of a task!

12.s:
taruṇas tava rūpeṇa careyaṃ pṛthivīm imām
jarāṃ tvayi samādhāya taṃ yaduḥ pratyuvāca ha //
12.d:
तरुणस् तव रूपेण चरेयं पृथिवीम् इमाम्
जरां त्वयि समाधाय तं यदुः प्रत्युवाच ह ॥
12.m: Young with your appearance, I would wander this earth, / having placed my old age on you.' To him Yadu replied:

12.s:
yadur uvāca
anirdiṣṭā mayā bhikṣā brāhmaṇasya pratiśrutā
anapākṛtya tāṃ rājan na grahīṣyāmi te jarām //
12.d:
यदुर् उवाच
अनिर्दिष्टा मया भिक्षा ब्राह्मणस्य प्रतिश्रुता
अनपाकृत्य तां राजन् न ग्रहीष्यामि ते जराम् ॥
12.m: Yadu said: / 'I have promised an unspecified alms-offering to a brāhmaṇa; / without fulfilling that, O king, I will not take your old age.

12.s:
jarāyāṃ bahavo doṣāḥ pānabhojanakāritāḥ
tasmāj jarāṃ na te rājan grahītum aham utsahe //
12.d:
जरायां बहवो दोषाः पानभोजनकारिताः
तस्माज् जरां न ते राजन् ग्रहीतुम् अहम् उत्सहे ॥
12.m: In old age there are many afflictions caused by eating and drinking; / therefore, O king, I am not able to take your old age.

12.s:
santi te bahavaḥ putrā mattaḥ priyatarā nṛpa
pratigrahītuṃ dharmajña putram anyaṃ vṛṇīṣva vai //
12.d:
सन्ति ते बहवः पुत्रा मत्तः प्रियतरा नृप
प्रतिग्रहीतुं धर्मज्ञ पुत्रम् अन्यं वृणीष्व वै ॥
12.m: You have many sons dearer to you than me, O king; / choose another son, O knower of dharma, to take it!'

12.s:
sa evam ukto yadunā rājā kopasamanvitaḥ
uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho yayātir garhayan sutam //
12.d:
स एवम् उक्तो यदुना राजा कोपसमन्वितः
उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो ययातिर् गर्हयन् सुतम् ॥
12.m: Being addressed thus by Yadu, the king, filled with anger, / that Yayāti, foremost among eloquent speakers, said, rebuking his son:

12.s:
yayātir uvāca
ka āśramas tavānyo 'sti ko vā dharmo vidhīyate
mām anādṛtya durbuddhe yad ahaṃ tava deśikaḥ //
12.d:
ययातिर् उवाच
क आश्रमस् तवान्यो ऽस्ति को वा धर्मो विधीयते
माम् अनादृत्य दुर्बुद्धे यद् अहं तव देशिकः ॥
12.m: Yayāti said: / 'What other stage of life is there for you? What dharma is prescribed for you, / that you disregard me, O fool, when I am your spiritual guide?'

12.s:
evam uktvā yaduṃ viprāḥ śaśāpainaṃ sa manyumān
arājyā te prajā mūḍha bhavitrīti na saṃśayaḥ //
12.d:
एवम् उक्त्वा यदुं विप्राः शशापैनं स मन्युमान्
अराज्या ते प्रजा मूढ भवित्रीति न संशयः ॥
12.m: Having spoken thus to Yadu, O vipras, he, full of fury, cursed him: / 'Your offspring, O fool, shall have no kingdom, of this there is no doubt!'

12.s:
druhyaṃ ca turvasuṃ caivāpy anuṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ
evam evābravīd rājā pratyākhyātaś ca tair api //
12.d:
द्रुह्यं च तुर्वसुं चैवाप्य् अनुं च द्विजसत्तमाः
एवम् एवाब्रवीद् राजा प्रत्याख्यातश् च तैर् अपि ॥
12.m: To Druhyu, Turvasu, and Anu also, O best of twice-borns, / the king spoke in the very same way, and he was refused by them as well.

12.s:
śaśāpa tān atikruddho yayātir aparājitaḥ
yathāvat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mayāsya dvijasattamāḥ //
12.d:
शशाप तान् अतिक्रुद्धो ययातिर् अपराजितः
यथावत् कथितं सर्वं मयास्य द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
12.m: Extremely enraged, the undefeated Yayāti cursed them. / Everything of this has been recounted properly by me, O best of twice-borns.

12.s:
evaṃ śaptvā sutān sarvāṃś caturaḥ purupūrvajān
tad eva vacanaṃ rājā purum apy āha bho dvijāḥ //
12.d:
एवं शप्त्वा सुतान् सर्वांश् चतुरः पुरुपूर्वजान्
तद् एव वचनं राजा पुरुम् अप्य् आह भो द्विजाः ॥
12.m: Having thus cursed all four sons who were elder to Puru, / the king spoke the very same words to Puru as well, O twice-borns:

12.s:
taruṇas tava rūpeṇa careyaṃ pṛthivīm imām
jarāṃ tvayi samādhāya tvaṃ puro yadi manyase //
12.d:
तरुणस् तव रूपेण चरेयं पृथिवीम् इमाम्
जरां त्वयि समाधाय त्वं पुरो यदि मन्यसे ॥
12.m: 'Young with your appearance, I would wander this earth, / having placed my old age on you, if you consent, O Puru.'

12.s:
sa jarāṃ pratijagrāha pituḥ puruḥ pratāpavān
yayātir api rūpeṇa puroḥ paryacaran mahīm //
12.d:
स जरां प्रतिजग्राह पितुः पुरुः प्रतापवान्
ययातिर् अपि रूपेण पुरोः पर्यचरन् महीम् ॥
12.m: The glorious Puru accepted the old age of his father; / and Yayāti, with the appearance of Puru, traversed the earth.

12.s:
sa mārgamāṇaḥ kāmānām antaṃ nṛpatisattamaḥ
viśvācyā sahito reme vane caitrarathe prabhuḥ //
12.d:
स मार्गमाणः कामानाम् अन्तं नृपतिसत्तमः
विश्वाच्या सहितो रेमे वने चैत्ररथे प्रभुः ॥
12.m: Seeking the limit of desires, that best of kings, / the powerful lord, took pleasure with Viśvācī in the Caitraratha forest.

12.s:
yadā ca tṛptaḥ kāmeṣu bhogeṣu ca narādhipaḥ
tadā puroḥ sakāśād vai svāṃ jarāṃ pratyapadyata //
12.d:
यदा च तृप्तः कामेषु भोगेषु च नराधिपः
तदा पुरोः सकाशाद् वै स्वां जरां प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
12.m: And when the ruler of men was sated with desires and pleasures, / he took back his own old age from Puru.

12.s:
yatra gāthā muniśreṣṭhā gītāḥ kila yayātinā
yābhiḥ pratyāharet kāmān sarvaśo 'ṅgāni kūrmavat //
12.d:
यत्र गाथा मुनिश्रेष्ठा गीताः किल ययातिना
याभिः प्रत्याहरेत् कामान् सर्वशो ऽङ्गानि कूर्मवत् ॥
12.m: Whereupon, O best of sages, verses were sung by Yayāti, / through which one should withdraw the senses completely, as a tortoise its limbs:

12.s:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate //
12.d:
न जातु कामः कामानाम् उपभोगेन शाम्यति
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ॥
12.m: 'Desire is never extinguished by the enjoyment of desires; / it only increases further, like fire fed with clarified butter.

12.s:
yat pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ
nālam ekasya tat sarvam iti kṛtvā na muhyati //
12.d:
यत् पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः
नालम् एकस्य तत् सर्वम् इति कृत्वा न मुह्यति ॥
12.m: Whatever rice, barley, gold, cattle, and women there are on earth / are not enough for even one man'—realizing this, one is not deluded.

12.s:
yadā bhāvaṃ na kurute sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam
karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
12.d:
यदा भावं न कुरुते सर्वभूतेषु पापकम्
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
12.m: When one harbors no sinful thought toward any living being / in deed, mind, or speech, then one attains Brahman.

12.s:
yadā tebhyo na bibheti yadā cāsmān na bibhyati
yadā necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
12.d:
यदा तेभ्यो न बिभेति यदा चास्मान् न बिभ्यति
यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
12.m: When one fears nothing, and when beings do not fear one, / when one neither desires nor hates, then one attains Brahman.

12.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ
yo 'sau prāṇāntiko rogas tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham //
12.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर् या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः
यो ऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस् तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥
12.m: That which is hard to renounce by the foolish, which does not age as one ages, / which is an incurable disease ending only with life—he who renounces that thirst finds happiness.

12.s:
jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ
dhanāśā jīvitāśā ca jīryato 'pi na jīryati //
12.d:
जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः
धनाशा जीविताशा च जीर्यतो ऽपि न जीर्यति ॥
12.m: Hair grows gray as a person grows old, teeth wear away as a person grows old, / but the longing for wealth and the longing for life do not grow old even as one grows old.

12.s:
yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham
tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām //
12.d:
यच् च कामसुखं लोके यच् च दिव्यं महत् सुखम्
तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हन्ति षोडशीं कलाम् ॥
12.m: Whatever pleasure of desire there is in the world, and whatever great heavenly bliss, / they are not worth a sixteenth part of the joy that comes from the destruction of thirst.

12.s:
evam uktvā sa rājarṣiḥ sadāraḥ prāviśad vanam
kālena mahatā cāyaṃ cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ //
12.d:
एवम् उक्त्वा स राजर्षिः सदारः प्राविशद् वनम्
कालेन महता चायं चचार विपुलं तपः ॥
12.m: Having spoken thus, that royal sage entered the forest with his wife; / and over a long time, he practiced severe austerity.

12.s:
bhṛgutuṅge gatiṃ prāpa tapaso 'nte mahāyaśāḥ
anaśnan deham utsṛjya sadāraḥ svargam āptavān //
12.d:
भृगुतुङ्गे गतिं प्राप तपसो ऽन्ते महायशाः
अनश्नन् देहम् उत्सृज्य सदारः स्वर्गम् आप्तवान् ॥
12.m: On the peak of Bhṛgutuṅga, the highly renowned [king] reached his goal at the end of his austerity; / casting off his body by fasting, he attained heaven along with his wife.

12.s:
tasya vaṃśe muniśreṣṭhāḥ pañca rājarṣisattamāḥ
yair vyāptā pṛthivī sarvā sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ //
12.d:
तस्य वंशे मुनिश्रेष्ठाः पञ्च राजर्षिसत्तमाः
यैर् व्याप्ता पृथिवी सर्वा सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः ॥
12.m: In his lineage, O best of sages, were five most excellent royal sages, / by whom the entire earth was pervaded, as if by the rays of the sun.

12.s:
yados tu vaṃśaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ rājasatkṛtam
yatra nārāyaṇo jajñe harir vṛṣṇikulodvahaḥ //
12.d:
यदोस् तु वंशं वक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं राजसत्कृतम्
यत्र नारायणो जज्ञे हरिर् वृष्णिकुलोद्वहः ॥
12.m: Now I shall tell the lineage of Yadu, honored by kings, listen: / in which Nārāyaṇa was born, Hari, the uplifter of the Vṛṣṇi race.

12.s:
susthaḥ prajāvān āyuṣmān kīrtimāṃś ca bhaven naraḥ
yayāticaritaṃ nityam idaṃ śṛṇvan dvijottamāḥ //
12.d:
सुस्थः प्रजावान् आयुष्मान् कीर्तिमांश् च भवेन् नरः
ययातिचरितं नित्यम् इदं शृण्वन् द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
12.m: A man will become sound in health, possessed of offspring, long-lived, and renowned, / listening constantly to this deed of Yayāti, O best of twice-born [sages].

13.s:
brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ
puror vaṃśaṃ vayaṃ sūta śrotum icchāma tattvataḥ
druhyasyānor yadoś caiva turvasoś ca pṛthak pṛthak //
13.d:
ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः
पुरोर् वंशं वयं सूत श्रोतुम् इच्छाम तत्त्वतः
द्रुह्यस्यानोर् यदोश् चैव तुर्वसोश् च पृथक् पृथक् ॥
13.m: The brāhmaṇas said: / We wish to hear truly, O sūta, the lineage of Puru, / and separately those of Druhyu, Anu, Yadu, and Turvasu.

13.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ muniśārdūlāḥ puror vaṃśaṃ mahātmanaḥ
vistareṇānupūrvyā ca prathamaṃ vadato mama //
13.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
शृणुध्वं मुनिशार्दूलाः पुरोर् वंशं महात्मनः
विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च प्रथमं वदतो मम ॥
13.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Listen, O tigers among sages, to the lineage of the great-souled Puru, / as I tell it first in detail and in proper order.

13.s:
puroḥ putraḥ suvīro 'bhūn manasyus tasya cātmajaḥ
rājā cābhayado nāma manasyor abhavat sutaḥ //
13.d:
पुरोः पुत्रः सुवीरो ऽभून् मनस्युस् तस्य चात्मजः
राजा चाभयदो नाम मनस्योर् अभवत् सुतः ॥
13.m: Puru's son was Suvīra, and his son was Manasyu; / and a king named Abhayada was the son of Manasyu.

13.s:
tathaivābhayadasyāsīt sudhanvā nāma pārthivaḥ
sudhanvanaḥ subāhuś ca raudrāśvas tasya cātmajaḥ //
13.d:
तथैवाभयदस्यासीत् सुधन्वा नाम पार्थिवः
सुधन्वनः सुबाहुश् च रौद्राश्वस् तस्य चात्मजः ॥
13.m: Likewise, Abhayada had a [son, a] ruler of the earth named Sudhanvan; / Sudhanvan's son was Subāhu, and his son was Raudrāśva.

13.s:
raudrāśvasya daśārṇeyuḥ kṛkaṇeyus tathaiva ca
kakṣeyusthaṇḍileyuś ca sannateyus tathaiva ca //
13.d:
रौद्राश्वस्य दशार्णेयुः कृकणेयुस् तथैव च
कक्षेयुस्थण्डिलेयुश् च सन्नतेयुस् तथैव च ॥
13.m: Raudrāśva's sons were Daśārṇeyu, Kṛkaṇeyu, / Kakṣeyu, Sthaṇḍileyu, and Sannateyu,

13.s:
ṛceyuś ca jaleyuś ca sthaleyuś ca mahābalaḥ
dhaneyuś ca vaneyuś ca putrakāś ca daśa striyaḥ //
13.d:
ऋचेयुश् च जलेयुश् च स्थलेयुश् च महाबलः
धनेयुश् च वनेयुश् च पुत्रकाश् च दश स्त्रियः ॥
13.m: Ṛceyu, Jaleyu, Sthaleyu of mighty strength, / Dhaneyu, and Vaneyu; and there were ten daughters [as well]:

13.s:
bhadrā śūdrā ca madrā ca śaladā maladā tathā
khaladā ca tato viprā naladā surasāpi ca //
13.d:
भद्रा शूद्रा च मद्रा च शलदा मलदा तथा
खलदा च ततो विप्रा नलदा सुरसापि च ॥
13.m: Bhadrā, Śūdrā, Madrā, Śaladā, Maladā, / Khaladā, and then Naladā, and Surasā,

13.s:
tathā gocapalā ca strīratnakūṭā ca tā daśa
ṛṣir jāto 'trivaṃśe ca tāsāṃ bhartā prabhākaraḥ //
13.d:
तथा गोचपला च स्त्रीरत्नकूटा च ता दश
ऋषिर् जातो ऽत्रिवंशे च तासां भर्ता प्रभाकरः ॥
13.m: and Gocapalā, and Ratnakūṭā—these ten women. / A sage born in the lineage of Atri was their husband, Prabhākara.

13.s:
bhadrāyāṃ janayām āsa sutaṃ somaṃ yaśasvinam
svarbhānunā hate sūrye patamāne divo mahīm //
13.d:
भद्रायां जनयाम् आस सुतं सोमं यशस्विनम्
स्वर्भानुना हते सूर्ये पतमाने दिवो महीम् ॥
13.m: Upon Bhadrā he begot a renowned son, Soma. / When the sun was struck by Svarbhānu and was falling from heaven to earth,

13.s:
tamobhibhūte loke ca prabhā yena pravartitā
svasti te 'stv iti coktvā vai patamāno divākaraḥ //
13.d:
तमोभिभूते लोके च प्रभा येन प्रवर्तिता
स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्व् इति चोक्त्वा वै पतमानो दिवाकरः ॥
13.m: and when the world was overcome by darkness, [Prabhākara] brought forth light. / And saying, 'May you have well-being!' to the falling sun,

13.s:
vacanāt tasya viprarṣer na papāta divo mahīm
atriśreṣṭhāni gotrāṇi yaś cakāra mahātapāḥ //
13.d:
वचनात् तस्य विप्रर्षेर् न पपात दिवो महीम्
अत्रिश्रेष्ठानि गोत्राणि यश् चकार महातपाः ॥
13.m: by the word of that twice-born sage, it did not fall from heaven to earth. / That sage of great austerity founded gotras superior to Atri's.

13.s:
yajñeṣv atrer balaṃ caiva devair yasya pratiṣṭhitam
sa tāsu janayām āsa putrikāsv ātmakāmajān //
13.d:
यज्ञेष्व् अत्रेर् बलं चैव देवैर् यस्य प्रतिष्ठितम्
स तासु जनयाम् आस पुत्रिकास्व् आत्मकामजान् ॥
13.m: The power of Atri in sacrifices was established by the gods; / he begot upon those daughters [of Raudrāśva] sons of his own desire:

13.s:
daśa putrān mahāsattvāṃs tapasy ugre ratāṃs tathā
te tu gotrakarā viprā ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ //
13.d:
दश पुत्रान् महासत्त्वांस् तपस्य् उग्रे रतांस् तथा
ते तु गोत्रकरा विप्रा ऋषयो वेदपारगाः ॥
13.m: ten sons of great nobility who were devoted to fierce austerity. / They were twice-born founders of gotras, sages who had mastered the Vedas,

13.s:
svastyātreyā iti khyātāḥ kiṃca tridhanavarjitāḥ
kakṣeyos tanayās tv āsaṃs traya eva mahārathāḥ //
13.d:
स्वस्त्यात्रेया इति ख्याताः किंच त्रिधनवर्जिताः
कक्षेयोस् तनयास् त्व् आसंस् त्रय एव महारथाः ॥
13.m: known as the Svastyātreyas, and free of the three types of wealth. / But Kakṣeyu had three sons, who were all great car-warriors:

13.s:
sabhānaraś cākṣuṣaś ca paramanyus tathaiva ca
sabhānarasya putras tu vidvān kālānalo nṛpaḥ //
13.d:
सभानरश् चाक्षुषश् च परमन्युस् तथैव च
सभानरस्य पुत्रस् तु विद्वान् कालानलो नृपः ॥
13.m: Sabhānara, Cākṣuṣa, and Paramanyu. / Sabhānara's son was the learned King Kālānala.

13.s:
kālānalasya dharmajñaḥ sṛñjayo nāma vai sutaḥ
sṛñjayasyābhavat putro vīro rājā puraṃjayaḥ //
13.d:
कालानलस्य धर्मज्ञः सृञ्जयो नाम वै सुतः
सृञ्जयस्याभवत् पुत्रो वीरो राजा पुरंजयः ॥
13.m: Kālānala's son was Sṛñjaya, knower of dharma; / Sṛñjaya's son was the heroic king Puraṃjaya.

13.s:
janamejayo muniśreṣṭhāḥ puraṃjayasuto 'bhavat
janamejayasya rājarṣer mahāśālo 'bhavat sutaḥ //
13.d:
जनमेजयो मुनिश्रेष्ठाः पुरंजयसुतो ऽभवत्
जनमेजयस्य राजर्षेर् महाशालो ऽभवत् सुतः ॥
13.m: Janamejaya, O best of sages, was the son of Puraṃjaya; / of the royal sage Janamejaya, Mahāśāla was the son.

13.s:
deveṣu sa parijñātaḥ pratiṣṭhitayaśā bhuvi
mahāmanā nāma suto mahāśālasya viśrutaḥ //
13.d:
देवेषु स परिज्ञातः प्रतिष्ठितयशा भुवि
महामना नाम सुतो महाशालस्य विश्रुतः ॥
13.m: Known among the gods, his fame was established on earth. / A renowned son of Mahāśāla was named Mahāmanas.

13.s:
jajñe vīraḥ suragaṇaiḥ pūjitaḥ sumahāmanāḥ
mahāmanās tu putrau dvau janayām āsa bho dvijāḥ //
13.d:
जज्ञे वीरः सुरगणैः पूजितः सुमहामनाः
महामनास् तु पुत्रौ द्वौ जनयाम् आस भो द्विजाः ॥
13.m: The heroic and high-minded [king] was born, honored by hosts of gods. / Mahāmanas begot two sons, O twice-born ones:

13.s:
uśīnaraṃ ca dharmajñaṃ titikṣuṃ ca mahābalam
uśīnarasya patnyas tu pañca rājarṣivaṃśajāḥ //
13.d:
उशीनरं च धर्मज्ञं तितिक्षुं च महाबलम्
उशीनरस्य पत्न्यस् तु पञ्च राजर्षिवंशजाः ॥
13.m: Uśīnara, knower of dharma, and Titikṣu of mighty strength. / Uśīnara had five wives born in the lineage of royal sages:

13.s:
nṛgā kṛmir navā darvā pañcamī ca dṛṣadvatī
uśīnarasya putrās tu pañca tāsu kulodvahāḥ //
13.d:
नृगा कृमिर् नवा दर्वा पञ्चमी च दृषद्वती
उशीनरस्य पुत्रास् तु पञ्च तासु कुलोद्वहाः ॥
13.m: Nṛgā, Kṛmi, Navā, Darvā, and Dṛṣadvatī as the fifth. / Uśīnara had five sons who carried forward the lineage through them,

13.s:
tapasā caiva mahatā jātā vṛddhasya cātmajāḥ
nṛgāyās tu nṛgaḥ putraḥ kṛmyāṃ kṛmir ajāyata //
13.d:
तपसा चैव महता जाता वृद्धस्य चात्मजाः
नृगायास् तु नृगः पुत्रः कृम्यां कृमिर् अजायत ॥
13.m: born through great austerity to him when he was aged: / Nṛgā's son was Nṛga, and upon Kṛmi, Kṛmi was born;

13.s:
navāyās tu navaḥ putro darvāyāḥ suvrato 'bhavat
dṛṣadvatyās tu saṃjajñe śibir auśīnaro nṛpaḥ //
13.d:
नवायास् तु नवः पुत्रो दर्वायाः सुव्रतो ऽभवत्
दृषद्वत्यास् तु संजज्ञे शिबिर् औशीनरो नृपः ॥
13.m: Navā's son was Nava, Darvā's was Suvrata, / and upon Dṛṣadvatī was born King Śibi Auśīnara.

13.s:
śibes tu śibayo viprā yaudheyās tu nṛgasya ha
navasya navarāṣṭraṃ tu kṛmes tu kṛmilā purī //
13.d:
शिबेस् तु शिबयो विप्रा यौधेयास् तु नृगस्य ह
नवस्य नवराष्ट्रं तु कृमेस् तु कृमिला पुरी ॥
13.m: From Śibi descended the Śibis, O twice-born ones; from Nṛga, the Yaudheyas; / of Nava, Navarāṣṭra; of Kṛmi, the city Kṛmilā;

13.s:
suvratasya tathāmbaṣṭhāḥ śibiputrān nibodhata
śibes tu śibayaḥ putrāś catvāro lokaviśrutāḥ //
13.d:
सुव्रतस्य तथाम्बष्ठाः शिबिपुत्रान् निबोधत
शिबेस् तु शिबयः पुत्राश् चत्वारो लोकविश्रुताः ॥
13.m: and of Suvrata, the Ambaṣṭhas. Learn now of Śibi's sons: / Śibi had four sons, world-renowned:

13.s:
vṛṣadarbhaḥ suvīraś ca kekayo madrakas tathā
teṣāṃ janapadāḥ sphītā kekayā madrakās tathā //
13.d:
वृषदर्भः सुवीरश् च केकयो मद्रकस् तथा
तेषां जनपदाः स्फीता केकया मद्रकास् तथा ॥
13.m: Vṛṣadarbha, Suvīra, Kekaya, and Madraka. / Their prosperous realms were the Kekayas and the Madrakas,

13.s:
vṛṣadarbhāḥ suvīrāś ca titikṣos tu prajās tv imāḥ
titikṣur abhavad rājā pūrvasyāṃ diśi bho dvijāḥ //
13.d:
वृषदर्भाः सुवीराश् च तितिक्षोस् तु प्रजास् त्व् इमाः
तितिक्षुर् अभवद् राजा पूर्वस्यां दिशि भो द्विजाः ॥
13.m: the Vṛṣadarbhas and the Suvīras. These are the offspring of Titikṣu: / Titikṣu became a king in the eastern quarter, O twice-born ones.

13.s:
uṣadratho mahāvīryaḥ phenas tasya suto 'bhavat
phenasya sutapā jajñe tataḥ sutapaso baliḥ //
13.d:
उषद्रथो महावीर्यः फेनस् तस्य सुतो ऽभवत्
फेनस्य सुतपा जज्ञे ततः सुतपसो बलिः ॥
13.m: His son was Uṣadratha of great prowess; Phena was his son; / to Phena was born Sutapas, and after Sutapas, Bali.

13.s:
jāto mānuṣayonau tu sa rājā kāñcaneṣudhiḥ
mahāyogī sa tu balir babhūva nṛpatiḥ purā //
13.d:
जातो मानुषयोनौ तु स राजा काञ्चनेषुधिः
महायोगी स तु बलिर् बभूव नृपतिः पुरा ॥
13.m: Born in a human womb, that king possessed golden quivers; / a great yogin, that Bali was a king in ancient times.

13.s:
putrān utpādayām āsa pañca vaṃśakarān bhuvi
aṅgaḥ prathamato jajñe vaṅgaḥ suhmas tathaiva ca //
13.d:
पुत्रान् उत्पादयाम् आस पञ्च वंशकरान् भुवि
अङ्गः प्रथमतो जज्ञे वङ्गः सुह्मस् तथैव च ॥
13.m: He fathered five sons who established lineages on earth: / Aṅga was born first, and Vaṅga and Suhma,

13.s:
puṇḍraḥ kaliṅgaś ca tathā bāleyaṃ kṣatram ucyate
bāleyā brāhmaṇāś caiva tasya vaṃśakarā bhuvi //
13.d:
पुण्ड्रः कलिङ्गश् च तथा बालेयं क्षत्रम् उच्यते
बालेया ब्राह्मणाश् चैव तस्य वंशकरा भुवि ॥
13.m: and Puṇḍra and Kaliṅga; they are called the Bāleya kṣatriyas. / There were also Bāleya brāhmaṇas who established his lineage on earth.

13.s:
baleś ca brahmaṇā datto varaḥ prītena bho dvijāḥ
mahāyogitvam āyuś ca kalpasya parimāṇataḥ //
13.d:
बलेश् च ब्रह्मणा दत्तो वरः प्रीतेन भो द्विजाः
महायोगित्वम् आयुश् च कल्पस्य परिमाणतः ॥
13.m: A boon was granted to Bali by Brahmā, pleased [with him], O twice-born ones: / the state of a great yogin, a lifespan for the duration of a kalpa,

13.s:
bale cāpratimatvaṃ vai dharmatattvārthadarśanam
saṃgrāme cāpy ajeyatvaṃ dharme caiva pradhānatām //
13.d:
बले चाप्रतिमत्वं वै धर्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शनम्
संग्रामे चाप्य् अजेयत्वं धर्मे चैव प्रधानताम् ॥
13.m: matchlessness in strength, perception of the true nature of dharma, / invincibility in battle, and supremacy in dharma,

13.s:
trailokyadarśanaṃ cāpi prādhānyaṃ prasave tathā
caturo niyatān varṇāṃs tvaṃ ca sthāpayiteti ca //
13.d:
त्रैलोक्यदर्शनं चापि प्राधान्यं प्रसवे तथा
चतुरो नियतान् वर्णांस् त्वं च स्थापयितेति च ॥
13.m: vision of the three worlds, preeminence in procreation, / and: 'You shall establish the four fixed classes.'

13.s:
ity ukto vibhunā rājā baliḥ śāntiṃ parāṃ yayau
kālena mahatā viprāḥ svaṃ ca sthānam upāgamat //
13.d:
इत्य् उक्तो विभुना राजा बलिः शान्तिं परां ययौ
कालेन महता विप्राः स्वं च स्थानम् उपागमत् ॥
13.m: Addressed thus by the Lord, King Bali attained supreme peace, / and in the course of time, O twice-born ones, he departed to his own realm.

13.s:
teṣāṃ janapadāḥ pañca aṅgā vaṅgāḥ sasuhmakāḥ
kaliṅgāḥ puṇḍrakāś caiva prajās tv aṅgasya sāṃpratam //
13.d:
तेषां जनपदाः पञ्च अङ्गा वङ्गाः ससुह्मकाः
कलिङ्गाः पुण्ड्रकाश् चैव प्रजास् त्व् अङ्गस्य सांप्रतम् ॥
13.m: Their five realms were Aṅga, Vaṅga, together with Suhma, / Kaliṅga, and Puṇḍra; and now [hear of] the offspring of Aṅga.

13.s:
aṅgaputro mahān āsīd rājendro dadhivāhanaḥ
dadhivāhanaputras tu rājā diviratho 'bhavat //
13.d:
अङ्गपुत्रो महान् आसीद् राजेन्द्रो दधिवाहनः
दधिवाहनपुत्रस् तु राजा दिविरथो ऽभवत् ॥
13.m: Aṅga had a great son, the lord of kings Dadhivāhana; / King Diviratha was the son of Dadhivāhana.

13.s:
putro divirathasyāsīc chakratulyaparākramaḥ
vidvān dharmaratho nāma tasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ //
13.d:
पुत्रो दिविरथस्यासीच् छक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः
विद्वान् धर्मरथो नाम तस्य चित्ररथः सुतः ॥
13.m: The son of Diviratha was equal in prowess to Śakra, / wise, named Dharmaratha; his son was Citraratha.

13.s:
tena dharmarathenātha tadā kālañjare girau
yajatā saha śakreṇa somaḥ pīto mahātmanā //
13.d:
तेन धर्मरथेनाथ तदा कालञ्जरे गिरौ
यजता सह शक्रेण सोमः पीतो महात्मना ॥
13.m: By that magnanimous Dharmaratha, performing sacrifice then on Mount Kālañjara, / soma was drunk together with Śakra.

13.s:
atha citrarathasyāpi putro daśaratho 'bhavat
lomapāda iti khyāto yasya śāntā sutābhavat //
13.d:
अथ चित्ररथस्यापि पुत्रो दशरथो ऽभवत्
लोमपाद इति ख्यातो यस्य शान्ता सुताभवत् ॥
13.m: Then of Citraratha too, Daśaratha was the son, / renowned as Lomapāda, whose daughter was Śāntā.

13.s:
tasya dāśarathir vīraś caturaṅgo mahāyaśāḥ
ṛṣyaśṛṅgaprasādena jajñe vaṃśavivardhanaḥ //
13.d:
तस्य दाशरथिर् वीरश् चतुरङ्गो महायशाः
ऋष्यशृङ्गप्रसादेन जज्ञे वंशविवर्धनः ॥
13.m: His heroic, renowned son Caturaṅga, / the increaser of his lineage, was born by the favor of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga.

13.s:
caturaṅgasya putras tu pṛthulākṣa iti smṛtaḥ
pṛthulākṣasuto rājā campo nāma mahāyaśāḥ //
13.d:
चतुरङ्गस्य पुत्रस् तु पृथुलाक्ष इति स्मृतः
पृथुलाक्षसुतो राजा चम्पो नाम महायशाः ॥
13.m: The son of Caturaṅga was known as Pṛthulākṣa; / the son of Pṛthulākṣa was the king named Campa of great fame.

13.s:
campasya tu purī campā yā māliny abhavat purā
pūrṇabhadraprasādena haryaṅgo 'sya suto 'bhavat //
13.d:
चम्पस्य तु पुरी चम्पा या मालिन्य् अभवत् पुरा
पूर्णभद्रप्रसादेन हर्यङ्गो ऽस्य सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
13.m: The city of Campa was Campā, which was formerly Mālinī; / through the favor of Pūrṇabhadra, Haryaṅga became his son.

13.s:
tato vaibhāṇḍakis tasya vāraṇaṃ śakravāraṇam
avatārayām āsa mahīṃ mantrair vāhanam uttamam //
13.d:
ततो वैभाण्डकिस् तस्य वारणं शक्रवारणम्
अवतारयाम् आस महीं मन्त्रैर् वाहनम् उत्तमम् ॥
13.m: Then the son of Vibhaṇḍaka, by mantras, brought down / Śakra's elephant to the earth as an excellent mount for him.

13.s:
haryaṅgasya sutas tatra rājā bhadrarathaḥ smṛtaḥ
putro bhadrarathasyāsīd bṛhatkarmā prajeśvaraḥ //
13.d:
हर्यङ्गस्य सुतस् तत्र राजा भद्ररथः स्मृतः
पुत्रो भद्ररथस्यासीद् बृहत्कर्मा प्रजेश्वरः ॥
13.m: The son of Haryaṅga there is remembered as King Bhadraratha; / the son of Bhadraratha was Bṛhatkarman, lord of creatures.

13.s:
bṛhaddarbhaḥ sutas tasya yasmāj jajñe bṛhanmanāḥ
bṛhanmanās tu rājendro janayām āsa vai sutam //
13.d:
बृहद्दर्भः सुतस् तस्य यस्माज् जज्ञे बृहन्मनाः
बृहन्मनास् तु राजेन्द्रो जनयाम् आस वै सुतम् ॥
13.m: His son was Bṛhaddarbha, from whom Bṛhanmanas was born; / and the excellent king Bṛhanmanas indeed fathered a son,

13.s:
nāmnā jayadrathaṃ nāma yasmād dṛḍharatho nṛpaḥ
āsīd dṛḍharathasyāpi viśvajij janamejayī //
13.d:
नाम्ना जयद्रथं नाम यस्माद् दृढरथो नृपः
आसीद् दृढरथस्यापि विश्वजिज् जनमेजयी ॥
13.m: named Jayadratha, from whom King Dṛḍharatha [was born]; / and of Dṛḍharatha, Janamejaya Viśvajit was [the son].

13.s:
dāyādas tasya vaikarṇo vikarṇas tasya cātmajaḥ
tasya putraśataṃ tv āsīd aṅgānāṃ kulavardhanam //
13.d:
दायादस् तस्य वैकर्णो विकर्णस् तस्य चात्मजः
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्व् आसीद् अङ्गानां कुलवर्धनम् ॥
13.m: His heir was Vaikarṇa, and Vikarṇa was his son; / he had a hundred sons, increasers of the Anga family.

13.s:
ete 'ṅgavaṃśajāḥ sarve rājānaḥ kīrtitā mayā
satyavratā mahātmānaḥ prajāvanto mahārathāḥ //
13.d:
एते ऽङ्गवंशजाः सर्वे राजानः कीर्तिता मया
सत्यव्रता महात्मानः प्रजावन्तो महारथाः ॥
13.m: All these kings born in the lineage of Aṅga have been narrated by me: / true to their vows, magnanimous, possessed of progeny, great chariot-warriors.

13.s:
ṛceyos tu muniśreṣṭhā raudrāśvatanayasya vai
śṛṇudhvaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi vaṃśaṃ rājñas tu bho dvijāḥ //
13.d:
ऋचेयोस् तु मुनिश्रेष्ठा रौद्राश्वतनयस्य वै
शृणुध्वं संप्रवक्ष्यामि वंशं राज्ञस् तु भो द्विजाः ॥
13.m: O best of sages, O twice-born ones, hear the royal lineage of Ṛceyu, / the son of Raudrāśva, which I will now proclaim!

13.s:
ṛceyos tanayo rājā matināro mahīpatiḥ
matinārasutās tv āsaṃs trayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ //
13.d:
ऋचेयोस् तनयो राजा मतिनारो महीपतिः
मतिनारसुतास् त्व् आसंस् त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः ॥
13.m: The son of Ṛceyu was King Matināra, lord of the earth; / and the sons of Matināra were three, exceedingly righteous:

13.s:
vasurodhaḥ pratirathaḥ subāhuś caiva dhārmikaḥ
sarve vedavidaś caiva brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ //
13.d:
वसुरोधः प्रतिरथः सुबाहुश् चैव धार्मिकः
सर्वे वेदविदश् चैव ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः ॥
13.m: Vasurodha, Pratiratha, and the righteous Subāhu, / all knowers of the Veda, devoted to the brahman, and speakers of truth.

13.s:
ilā nāma tu yasyāsīt kanyā vai munisattamāḥ
brahmavādiny adhistrī sā taṃsus tām abhyagacchata //
13.d:
इला नाम तु यस्यासीत् कन्या वै मुनिसत्तमाः
ब्रह्मवादिन्य् अधिस्त्री सा तंसुस् ताम् अभ्यगच्छत ॥
13.m: O best of sages, he who had a daughter named Ilā, / that woman was an exponent of the Veda; Taṃsu approached her.

13.s:
taṃsoḥ suto 'tha rājarṣir dharmanetraḥ pratāpavān
brahmavādī parākrāntas tasya bhāryopadānavī //
13.d:
तंसोः सुतो ऽथ राजर्षिर् धर्मनेत्रः प्रतापवान्
ब्रह्मवादी पराक्रान्तस् तस्य भार्योपदानवी ॥
13.m: The son of Taṃsu was the royal sage Dharmanetra, powerful, / an exponent of the Veda, valiant; his wife was Upadānavī.

13.s:
upadānavī tataḥ putrāṃś caturo 'janayac chubān
duṣyantam atha suṣmantaṃ pravīram anaghaṃ tathā //
13.d:
उपदानवी ततः पुत्रांश् चतुरो ऽजनयच् छुबान्
दुष्यन्तम् अथ सुष्मन्तं प्रवीरम् अनघं तथा ॥
13.m: Then Upadānavī bore four auspicious sons: / Duṣyanta, then Suṣmanta, Pravīra, and Anagha.

13.s:
duṣyantasya tu dāyādo bharato nāma vīryavān
sa sarvadamano nāma nāgāyutabalo mahān //
13.d:
दुष्यन्तस्य तु दायादो भरतो नाम वीर्यवान्
स सर्वदमनो नाम नागायुतबलो महान् ॥
13.m: The heir of Duṣyanta was the powerful Bharata, / he was named Sarvadamana, great, with the strength of ten thousand elephants.

13.s:
cakravartī suto jajñe duṣyantasya mahātmanaḥ
śakuntalāyāṃ bharato yasya nāmnā tu bhāratāḥ //
13.d:
चक्रवर्ती सुतो जज्ञे दुष्यन्तस्य महात्मनः
शकुन्तलायां भरतो यस्य नाम्ना तु भारताः ॥
13.m: A universal emperor, the son of the magnanimous Duṣyanta, Bharata, / was born of Śakuntalā, after whose name the descendants of Bharata are called.

13.s:
bharatasya vinaṣṭeṣu tanayeṣu mahīpateḥ
mātṝṇāṃ tu prakopeṇa mayā tat kathitaṃ purā //
13.d:
भरतस्य विनष्टेषु तनयेषु महीपतेः
मातॄणां तु प्रकोपेण मया तत् कथितं पुरा ॥
13.m: When the sons of King Bharata perished / through the wrath of their mothers, as was told by me formerly,

13.s:
bṛhaspater aṅgirasaḥ putro vipro mahāmuniḥ
ayājayad bharadvājo mahadbhiḥ kratubhir vibhuḥ //
13.d:
बृहस्पतेर् अङ्गिरसः पुत्रो विप्रो महामुनिः
अयाजयद् भरद्वाजो महद्भिः क्रतुभिर् विभुः ॥
13.m: the brahmin sage, the mighty and great sage Bharadvāja, / the son of Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa, officiated at great sacrifices for him.

13.s:
pūrvaṃ tu vitathe tasya kṛte vai putrajanmani
tato 'tha vitatho nāma bharadvājāt suto 'bhavat //
13.d:
पूर्वं तु वितथे तस्य कृते वै पुत्रजन्मनि
ततो ऽथ वितथो नाम भरद्वाजात् सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
13.m: Since formerly the birth of his sons had been rendered futile, / then a son named Vitatha was born from Bharadvāja.

13.s:
tato 'tha vitathe jāte bharatas tu divaṃ yayau
vitathaṃ cābhiṣicyātha bharadvājo vanaṃ yayau //
13.d:
ततो ऽथ वितथे जाते भरतस् तु दिवं ययौ
वितथं चाभिषिच्याथ भरद्वाजो वनं ययौ ॥
13.m: Then, once Vitatha was born, Bharata went to heaven; / and having consecrated Vitatha, Bharadvāja went to the forest.

13.s:
sa cāpi vitathaḥ putrāñ janayām āsa pañca vai
suhotraṃ ca suhotāraṃ gayaṃ gargaṃ tathaiva ca //
13.d:
स चापि वितथः पुत्राञ् जनयाम् आस पञ्च वै
सुहोत्रं च सुहोतारं गयं गर्गं तथैव च ॥
13.m: And that Vitatha fathered five sons indeed: / Suhotra, Suhotṛ, Gaya, and likewise Garga,

13.s:
kapilaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ suhotrasya sutadvayam
kāśikaṃ ca mahāsatyaṃ tathā gṛtsamatiṃ nṛpam //
13.d:
कपिलं च महात्मानं सुहोत्रस्य सुतद्वयम्
काशिकं च महासत्यं तथा गृत्समतिं नृपम् ॥
13.m: and the magnanimous Kapila. Suhotra had two sons: / Kāśika of great truth, and King Gṛtsamati.

13.s:
tathā gṛtsamateḥ putrā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ
kāśikasya tu kāśeyaḥ putro dīrghatapās tathā //
13.d:
तथा गृत्समतेः पुत्रा ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया विशः
काशिकस्य तु काशेयः पुत्रो दीर्घतपास् तथा ॥
13.m: From Gṛtsamati came sons who were brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas; / the son of Kāśika was Kāśeya, and also Dīrghatapas.

13.s:
babhūva dīrghatapaso vidvān dhanvantariḥ sutaḥ
